Repeat the 10-minute schedule 24 times; inspect cumulative results after one, two and three hours and decide at four hours. Preparation, warm-up and final comparison are outside the observation. No automatic extension or rerun.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-15. The later integrated 24-hour campaign is Backlog M66 after G8 confirms the required Ansible tools are ready. It does not block closure after G6 succeeds.
- The completed production scope retains its acceptance and implementation authorization of 2026-10-11. Decision Date: 2026-10-15. Direct execution of the accepted stress preparation, bounded preflight and conditional four-hour run is authorized. Preserve existing guests and evidence; no automatic retry or extension.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-11. The margin is a time with a floor of 1.0 s, not a multiplier of the expected sample count; the old multiplier key is dropped rather than kept as an alias.

| 0-1 minute | No injected delay; verify live input and writes |
| 1-5 minutes | Repeated 500 ms requested delay, exactly once per eligible actual pass |
| 5-9 minutes | Repeated 800 ms requested delay, exactly once per eligible actual pass |
| 9-10 minutes | Remove injection and confirm continued writes |

Requested 500/800 ms delay does not prove that every buffer remained within its margin. Retain actual swap intervals, scheduling/queue time and input bursts. Any loss in the positive observation prevents an overall Passed result. An exceeded margin remains visible as a limit condition and is not automatically proof of an incorrect sizing fix.

All 903 PVs require registration, active-input and counter coverage. Independent actual-input/unreduced-PB comparisons cover all 110 fast PVs; the remaining 793 PVs have counter/input-activity checks. Capture actual incoming events before the engine buffer, independently of stored output; compare timestamps including nanoseconds, values, status, severity, order and event multiplicities. Counter resets or decreases remain continuity findings and cannot be interpreted as zero loss. Preserve or read the real unreduced output before intentional ETL reduction/deletion. Retrieval deduplication, reduced counts and configured frequency multiplied by elapsed time are not actual input evidence. Do not claim exact value-level preservation of all 903 PVs.

##### Measured Stress Coverage

Assign each actual writer pass to the half-open phase window containing its monotonic start time. A pass is eligible when it starts inside a 500 or 800 ms phase after all 903 PVs are registered, has a native PB write and has complete pass, write and swap evidence. Keep every started pass in the record; an incomplete pass is a coverage gap, not an eligibility exclusion. Inject exactly once per eligible pass and never in passes assigned to baseline or recovery. At phase boundaries, finish the assigned pass without injecting a second time.

Alternate the selected native write between the first and last observed write positions in consecutive eligible passes, preserving actual write order and recording the selected PV and write position. Repeating a delay at an unchanged position does not establish repeated buffer pressure. Preflight must demonstrate this selection mechanism; a requested delay or an append-call count alone is insufficient.

Freeze the stress target list before the main run. Include all 110 fast PVs unless the first native write belongs to a fast PV whose swap necessarily precedes the injection. Only that one identified PV may be exempt from the stress-count requirement, leaving at least 109 targets; retain its all-PV loss checks and exact input/PB comparison. Do not select targets or exemptions from main-run outcomes.

A qualifying 500 ms exposure requires an observed filesystem-write delay of at least 500 ms, a consecutive swap interval of at least 10.4 s and at most 11.0 s, and 104-110 independently captured incoming events between those swaps. A qualifying 800 ms exposure requires at least 800 ms observed write delay, a swap interval of at least 10.7 s and at most 11.0 s, and 107-110 incoming events. Use monotonic engine-arrival/swap times for these measurements; retain IOC timestamps separately for PB comparison. Attribute each exposure to the delayed pass and its assigned phase.

Every target must receive at least one qualifying exposure of each level in each 10-minute cycle: at least 24 at 500 ms and 24 at 800 ms over four hours. The preflight requires at least one of each level per target. Report the per-PV/per-cycle counts, actual intervals, input counts and injection evidence. Fewer exposures means Incomplete even if loss counters remain zero. Keep all other intervals, including intervals above 11.0 s or inputs above capacity, in the overall record; they cannot erase observed loss or manufacture Passed.

##### Bounded Preflight

Allow one preflight attempt with a 1200-second monotonic deadline from the first fixture-registration or probe action after deployment. Registration, effective-configuration checks and complete capture must become ready within its first 300 seconds. After readiness, observe 120 seconds without injection, 120 seconds with the 500 ms schedule and 120 seconds with the 800 ms schedule. Require zero buffer-full counter increase and complete actual-input/PB matches in these normal and within-margin stages, plus the per-target measured exposures defined above.

Before the expected-loss control, disable injection and drain native writes beyond the recorded input cutoffs of the normal/500/800 ms stages. Complete and freeze those stages' input/PB comparisons before introducing intentional loss. Retain all intervening recovery inputs in the subsequent full preflight comparison so a delayed drop cannot be misclassified as a previous-stage loss or disappear from the evidence.

Then inject one observed filesystem-write delay of at least 1500 ms at the first native write of one pass, preserving the real IOC, engine, writer and PB path. This deliberately exceeds the configured margin: require at least one fast PV to have a positive buffer-full counter delta and an equal independently measured missing-event count in native PB after final writes/flush. Reconcile every fast PV; do not accept counter-only evidence or a comparator failure as successful loss detection. This expected-loss control is a separate preflight result, never part of the four-hour zero-loss acceptance.

Complete capture, native flush/decode, comparisons and the preflight verdict within the same 1200-second deadline. Passed requires every normal, measured-stress and expected-loss check. Unexpected loss in a normal/within-margin stage is a failed check; absent loss in the expected-loss control or missing coverage/evidence is Incomplete; record collector/evaluator errors separately. On any unmet condition or timeout, disable injection, retain originals, report the blocking finding and do not start the main run. No automatic retry or extension.

After Passed, start the main observation in a fresh engine execution with the same verified build, fixture and effective configuration, a new capture boundary and recorded initial counters. The preflight's expected losses remain preserved under its own process identity; a restart is not a reset within the main observation. Require continuous engine/counter identity throughout the subsequent four hours.

#### M49 - Engine shutdown polls the CA command queue at its own cadence

Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #32 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/32)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

`JCACommandThread.shutdown()` slept a full second before its first look at the command queue, so an engine with the default ten command threads took at least 10 s to stop although the destroy command drains within one 100 ms cycle; every unit test that shuts a `ConfigServiceForTests` down paid it. Out of scope: the remaining long tests (M50); shutting the command threads down in parallel.

- The default unit test set passes locally in under 15 min on the host that took 35 min.
- The CI run of the change passes.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- Decision Date: 2026-10-11. Keep the sequential shutdown and the condition; change only the first-check order and the polling interval.

#### M56 - Menu by task and console pages

Origin: daff1b7 / M56
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #38 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/38)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

A first use of the management interface of M47 at fcf01d9c, on a local appliance with the soft IOC of the book figures, found the menu out of step with the pages. Home and Reports open the same Browse PVs page in the same state: `reports.html` forwards to `index.html` (`js/forward.js`), and the reports are the **Show** list of the Find panel, which the entry neither selects nor opens. Metrics, Storage and Appliances all open the System tabs (`metrics.html` to `operations.html`, `storage.html` to `operations.html#stores`, `appliance.html` to `system.html`). No entry shows where the user is: `main.css` styles `ul.mainmenu li a.active`, no code sets it, and the entries point at forwarding pages that never match the page in view; only the System tabs mark the current tab. The System pages read as a report: headings phrased as questions, a paragraph under each, and a "What it means" column with one or two sentences on each of the nine Overview rows (`meaning` in `js/system.js`), which widens the table and makes it scroll sideways on a phone. The page stylesheets set most text in fixed pixels below the 15 px body: 12 to 13 px in `browse.css`, `system.css`, `integration.css` and `viewer.css`, 11 to 12 px for the chart axes and tooltip in `chart.css`; fixed pixels also ignore the browser's font size. Help opens `api/index.html`, the generated mgmt API reference (92 calls), and no console page links to the operator pages of the book. The Integration page has two Channel Archiver sections and an external data server section with the types `CA_XMLRPC` and `ARCHAPPL_PBRAW`. A full integration run on 2026-10-12 (110 tests, 2 h 36 min, Tomcat 9.0.121, softIocPVX 7.0.10) failed four: `MgmtPageLinksTest`, since the forwarding pages of M47 carry no Help link; `IPApplianceXMLTest`, whose assert looks for the text `archstatpVNames` of the pre-M47 home page; and `LocalhostApplianceXMLTest` and `FQDNApplianceXMLTest`, which could not start their Tomcat because the Tomcat of the failed `IPApplianceXMLTest` was left running on ports 17665 and 16670: when a test fails after `TomcatSetup` has started Tomcat, nothing stops it.

##### Scope

The menu and page frame of D38, the Integration change of D39, and the console rule of D38 on the System pages, with the book pages and tests that describe them.

- Menu entries Archive PVs, Browse PVs, System, Help and Analyzer, each opening its page and marking the page in view; Archive PVs and Browse PVs open `index.html` and Analyzer opens the viewer of M47 until M57 and M58 give them their own pages.
- The old addresses forward outside the menu, the Reports address with the Show list open.
- System: the explanations behind an information control (an `i` button) opened by a click (also on touch screens), state first; the external Archiver Appliance servers under System; the Channel Archiver sections and the `CA_XMLRPC` type removed from the interface.
- A System view drawn with D3: a treemap (`d3-hierarchy`) of the stored data and the event rate by PV name prefix in the Stores section of Operations. The stacked areas of the event rate and the stored data over time are in M61.
- Text sizes in rem across the page stylesheets, `chart.css` and `main.css`, on one scale (root 16 px): body 1rem, secondary text 0.9375rem, labels, table headings and chart ticks 0.875rem, headings 1.25rem to 1.375rem; no text below 14 px.
- Help opens the console help page of D42: one section per menu entry, the API reference as an entry under it, and a link to the book.
- `MgmtPageLinksTest` checks the pages of the new menu and the forwarding of the old addresses; `IPApplianceXMLTest` checks the home page by a marker of the shipped page; `TomcatSetup` stops the Tomcats it started when a test fails, so one failure does not take down the tests after it; `operating.md` and `interface.md` describe the new menu.

Out of scope: the Archive PVs and Browse PVs pages and the analyzer themselves (M57, M58); the chart component (M59); the server calls of the Channel Archiver parts, which stay.

##### Completion Criteria

- Each menu entry opens its page and is marked while that page is in view; each old address forwards to its place.
- The System pages show each measure's state without standing explanation text, and each explanation opens from its information control by a click.
- The external Archiver Appliance servers can be listed, added and removed under System; no page offers a Channel Archiver section or the `CA_XMLRPC` type.
- No text of the console or the viewer is set in fixed pixels, and no rendered text is below 14 px at the default browser font size.
- Help opens the console help page; each information control opens its card, which links to its section; the page reaches the API reference and links to the book.
- `MgmtPageLinksTest`, the three `appxml` tests and the default suite pass; a test that fails after Tomcat started leaves no Tomcat running; the book describes the menu as shipped.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- D38: console pages and the menu by task.
- D39: the Channel Archiver parts and the external Archiver Appliance servers.
- D41: the header frame, its two blocks and the default site logo.
- D42: the console help page.
- Decision Date 2026-10-13: the information control is a small circled `i` button with a 32 px tap area after the item name; a click or Enter opens a card with the meaning, where to act and a link into the help page, Escape or a click outside closes it. It replaces the standing "What it means" column and the sentence under the System headline.
- Decision Date 2026-10-13: the stacked areas of the event rate and the stored data by component or store leave this item for M61. The appliance keeps no history of these values (only the process heap series), so M56 draws the treemap from the current reports and M61 gives the history through archived status PVs.
- Decision Date 2026-10-13: the text sizes are one rem scale with 14 px as the smallest; the Help entry opens `help.html`, a usage guide of each page by task, not a copy of the book.

#### M57 - Archive PVs page

Origin: daff1b7 / M57
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #38 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/38)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The Browse PVs page joins adding PVs with finding archived PVs in one input. Find searches the names the appliance holds; adding registers a name on the control system network. The **Archive** offer appears in the result area only when Find matches no archived PV and the whole text is a valid PV name (`renderArchiveOffer` in `js/browse.js`), so no visible entry names the task, and the offer follows a half-typed name: typing `SR:BEAM` on the way to `SR:BEAM:CURRENT` offers `Archive SR:BEAM…`, and selecting it files a request for a name that does not exist, which stays in Initial sampling. Its trailing `…` reads as a cut-off name. A list of names pasted into Find (`<input id="q" type="search">`) is joined into one line, and the dialog takes one name (`openArchiveDialog([text])`) although the dialog code, `api.archivePVs` and the `archivePV` POST take a list; the dialog does not read the answer ("Archive request submitted", "Already submitted") and shows only a failed request. Stopping a PV in Initial sampling through the bulk actions pauses and then calls `deletePV`, whose `deleteSinglePV` answers HTTP 400 for a PV without a `PVTypeInfo`, and the page shows only "the server could not complete the request (HTTP 400)" (from reading the code). The only cancel of a pending request, **Abort the request** (`abortArchivingPV`), is in the Detail area at the bottom of the page for the first selected PV; the bulk actions under Scan have none.

##### Scope

The Archive PVs page of D38.

- An entry for adding PVs, apart from Find, that takes one name or a pasted list of a few to a few tens of names, one per line, and shows the answer for each name; larger requests use the `archivePV` call.
- A folded sampling choice with the method, the period, the policy (from `getPolicyList`) and the controlling PV, empty by default so that the policy decides.
- No archive offer for text the user is still typing.
- A label for the dialog control that does not read as a truncated name.
- Actions on each row of the PV list, for the PV's state: cancel for a pending request; pause or resume and stop for an archived PV.
- In the bulk actions, the cancel of pending requests offered last, and a stop that handles a pending PV by cancelling it or names the reason it cannot proceed.
- The book pages for adding and controlling PVs.

Out of scope: the check of a name on the network and the pause and hold of a pending request (M60); finding and plotting (M58).

##### Completion Criteria

- A pasted list of names is archived from the page and the page shows each name's answer.
- Typing a name shows no archive offer until the user asks for one.
- One PV is paused, resumed, stopped or cancelled from its row; a pending request is cancelled from the bulk actions; stopping a pending PV does not end in a bare HTTP status.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the page as shipped.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M56: the menu entry and page frame.
- D38: console pages.
- Decision Date 2026-10-12: the page takes lists of a few to a few tens of names; larger requests use the `archivePV` call.
- Decision Date 2026-10-13: one multi-line input takes one name or a list, one name per line, so a single name and a pasted list are the same action. The sampling is not preset to Monitor and 1 s: by default the site policy decides each PV's method and period, as the plain Archive button of the earlier interface did, and the method, the period, the policy and the controlling PV are a folded choice that applies to every name. The table below the input lists the PVs requested in this visit only, with the answer of the request, the state read back from the appliance, what the policy chose once sampling has started, and the actions of the state (cancel for a pending request, pause or resume and stop for an archived PV). Basis: the interface of the archiver before this rework, the upstream user guide, and the batch add of Tango HDB++ and the named sampling groups of Ignition, which apply one setting to a batch and leave per-item tuning to the row.

Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-13: the owner accepted the layout of the clickable mockup: one multi-line input, a folded sampling choice that leaves the decision to the site policy, and a table of the PVs requested in this visit with the state of each and the actions of its state
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-13, the owner directed the implementation of the accepted plan, in small steps that are tested and shown one by one
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

The page posts the names to `archivePV` as a list with the choice, shows the answer of each name, and reads the state of each requested PV with `getPVStatus`; a pending request is cancelled with `abortArchivingPV`; a pause, resume or stop uses the calls of the Browse PVs page, and a stop on a pending PV cancels it and says so.

#### M58 - Browse PVs page

Origin: daff1b7 / M58
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The hint above Find reads "Words in any order, case ignored" in every mode; Glob (the whole name, `*` and `?`) and Regex (any part of the name, `^` and `$` to anchor) have no explanation on the page. The page lists the PVs of a search as a Scan list (State, PV, a trend of the chosen range, the value now, the last event) with bulk actions under it, draws the ticked PVs in the Inspect area, and shows one PV at a time in a Detail area below; its State column is empty for a PV that is archived normally. The problems of the data viewer the page opens belong to the analyzer row.

##### Scope

The Browse PVs page of D38 and D40; the analyzer it opens is M62, and the chart it draws is the simple form of M59.

- The Browse PVs page, from the mockup the owner approved on 2026-10-14:
  - Find with an explanation of the three search modes that opens from an information button and closes with Esc, its Close button or a click outside, the focus returning to the button.
  - A PV ticked in the list adds a row to the table of PVs; the Plot box of a row draws that PV in the chart above the table, at most 5 at a time, the other boxes disabled at 5 with a short reason in their title and the explanation in the information card.
  - Table columns: Plot, PV, Protocol (CA or PVA, empty for a PV that is not archived), State (the state word of the PV with a mark and the number of lost events when it is above zero, the sum of `eventsDropped` of the three reports; a PV is in its normal state when its status is `Being archived` and none of the three reports lists it; the column is shown only while a PV is not in its normal state), Trend (a small line of the chosen range, as the Scan list of today draws it, for every PV of the table whether or not its Plot box is on), Value (aligned on the decimal point, with its unit; an array PV reads `array of N`), Last event (the date and time of the sample that Value shows, which is the time of the data, written in the zone chosen for the page, which is the time zone of the browser until M67 gives the choice), Std dev (only while the standard deviation band of the chart is on), Actions and a Details button.
  - The bulk actions of today's page stay under the table, for the ticked PVs: Pause all selected…, Resume all selected… and Stop archiving all selected…, each asking first, and the link Open all selected in the analyzer, which opens every ticked PV (not only the plotted ones) in the analyzer through `analyzer.html`, as the link of the chart does.
  - Actions in the row, by the state of the PV: Pause (Resume when paused) and a More menu with Change sampling, Maintenance and Stop archiving for a PV that is archived or paused; Cancel request for a pending request; a link to the Archive PVs page for a PV that is not archived. Stop archiving and Maintenance open a window that states the consequence before they act (a stop pauses the PV, removes it from the archiver, and keeps the stored data unless the user also chooses to delete it; a change of type asks for a confirmation that a backup exists). The calls are those of the Browse PVs page today.
  - The Details window, in groups, from `getPVStatus`, `getPVTypeInfo` and `getPVDetails`: how it is stored (appliance, sampling, policy, event and storage rate, growth, the time at which the archiver last passed the data to the short term store), amount, connection (with the time at which the archiver last received an event and the time of the data of the last event), lost events by cause, who reads it, the PV itself (data type, units, precision, display, control, warning and alarm limits, record type, archived fields, creation), and the moves between stores STS, MTS and LTS with the last and next run. A name the calls do not hold reads "not provided" (the unit and the host of a PVA PV); a value that is present and empty (the unit of a CA record without EGU), a pair of display, control, warning or alarm limits that are both 0 and a limit that is NaN read "not set", for a PVA PV and a CA PV alike. A time is shown as the server writes it, a string in the time zone of the server with its abbreviation (`Never` when there is no time, and `N/A` for the time of the data of an event that has not arrived), and is not converted before M67 and M70 (the epoch seconds of the server); each time is shown with the name that `getPVDetails` gives it (for example "When did we receive the last event?") under the heading of its kind as `docs/time-handling.md` defines it: the time of the data of the last event, the time at which the archiver received the last event, the time at which it last passed the data to the short term store, the last and the next run of the moves between stores, and the times of the connection, of the settings of the PV and of the last request for its data; the fields `Last monitor received at`, `Last monitor event timestamp` and `Daily metadata last saved at` are not shown.
  - The chart, built by M59 in its simple form and drawn on this page above the table: one Y axis per unit with its own automatic range, a drag along an axis choosing that axis's range, a drag over the plot choosing the time range, a double-click returning, the axes split between the left and the right of the plot (the first half on the left), a legend under the chart that names each PV with its line style and unit and whose items hide and show a line, a hover tooltip with the date and time and the value of each PV with its unit, a Y projection with its mean line and a table of basic statistics, and a Chart options panel for the line (step, straight, smooth, points only), the Y scale (linear, symmetric log, log, square root), sample marks, a running average and a standard deviation band over a window of samples; an Enlarge chart button opens the chart with its options in a large window.
  - The information card closes with Esc, its Close button and a click outside; the Details window and the windows of the actions close with Esc, their Close button and a click outside; the Enlarge chart window, which fills the browser window, closes with Esc and its Close button; the Options panel opens and closes with its Options button; the focus returns to the control that opened each.
  - The range strip above every chart, built in the chart component (`staticcontent/js/aa/chart.js`, `css/chart.css`) so that the Browse PVs page and the System charts share it: a line that is always there, holding the time window written as an interval with its date and time, `[from, to]` (a bracket includes the data at that end and a parenthesis leaves it out), the controls Earlier and Later (Earlier also works before a window is chosen, from the window of the range buttons `10m` to `7d`, so that a window can be walked back) and Back to the selected range as icons with a tooltip that stays inside the chart box, one control for each value axis that names its unit, shows the range chosen on it and returns it to the automatic range, a control that resets the window and every range, and an information control; the explanations are in its card. The strip of a System chart has the window as an interval, the control of each unit and the control that resets the ranges, and no Earlier, Later or Back to the selected range: a System chart shows every value its process has collected, at most 24 hours of one point a minute, and nothing older is stored (decision of 2026-10-16).
  - The Refresh control beside the range buttons: Off, 10 s, 30 s (the default) and 1 min; it acts on the chart and the table together, Off stops the automatic refresh and a button refreshes once, "Updated" with the time of the last refresh is written beside it, a window that does not end now is not refreshed and the control is dim, and a hidden browser tab pauses the refresh.
  - Open in the analyzer: a link to `analyzer.html` built from the plotted PVs (`pv`, repeated) and the time window (`from`, `to` in ISO form, the parameters the viewer reads today; the address of the page itself keeps its `from` and `to` in epoch milliseconds); the options chosen on the page are added to the address by M62, which defines their parameters.
- The book pages for finding PVs and the Browse PVs page, and the Browse PVs section of the Help page of the console (`help.html`), which names the Scan list, the Detail area and their buttons today.

Out of scope: the chart component (M59); the analyzer page, options and address (M62); adding PVs (M57).

##### Completion Criteria

- Each search mode's explanation opens from the page.
- A PV ticked in the list has a row with its trend of the chosen range, also when its Plot box is off; its Plot box draws it, at five the other Plot boxes are disabled with a short reason, and a PV of another unit gets its own axis with its own range.
- The table has the columns of the Scope: Protocol reads CA for a PV served over CA and PVA for one served over PVA, Value is aligned on the decimal point with its sign and its unit (an array PV reads `array of N`), and Last event is the date and time of the sample that Value shows, which is the time of the data and not the time at which the archiver received it.
- A row of a PV that is not archived has no Pause and no More menu, and carries a link to the Archive PVs page with the name of the PV in its address, as the link under Find does.
- The actions of a PV are in its row for its state: Pause or Resume, the More menu, and Cancel request for a pending request; each is read back from `getPVStatus`, and Stop archiving and Maintenance state the consequence before they act.
- Each time in the Details window is the string that `getPVDetails` returns for the same PV, unconverted, and is shown with the name that `getPVDetails` gives it under the heading of its kind (the time of the data, received, recorded, moved, or a time of the connection, of the settings or of a request).
- The Details window shows the groups of the Scope for a CA PV and for a PVA PV, reading "not provided" for a name the calls do not hold and "not set" for a value that is present and empty and for limits that are both 0 or NaN, and a PV with lost events shows the mark in its row.
- Each plotted PV is named in the legend under the chart and a click on its item hides and shows its line; the tooltip shows the date and time and each PV's value (the behavior of the component of M59, observed on this page).
- A range chosen with the mouse on the plot and on an axis changes the view, the Projection tab with its statistics, the Distribution panel and the Summary of the chart, and a double-click returns (the behavior of the component of M59, observed on this page).
- The options of the page (the Options button, tab Chart) change the chart: Line (Step, Straight, Smooth, Points) and Y scale (Linear, Symmetric log, Log, Square root) are followed by the drawn lines and axes (the behavior of the component of M59, observed on this page).
- Each card and window closes as the Scope says (Esc, its Close button, and a click outside where there is an outside), and the focus returns to the control that opened it.
- Open in the analyzer opens the analyzer with the plotted PVs and the time window of the chart.
- The State column is absent while every PV of the table is in its normal state and present, with the lost-events mark, when one is not; the Std dev column appears only while the standard deviation band of the chart is on.
- The bulk actions Pause all selected…, Resume all selected… and Stop archiving all selected… each ask first and act on the ticked PVs, and the link Open all selected in the analyzer opens every ticked PV in the analyzer.
- The address of the page (the part after `#`) carries `pv` for the ticked PVs and `plot` for the PVs whose Plot box is on, and keeps `q`, `mode`, `range`, `report`, `from` and `to` as today, so that the Operations links and the old addresses that forward to the page open it as they do; the link into the analyzer is built from `plot`.
- The range strip is above the chart of the page and above the System charts: the window is written as an interval on a 24 hour clock, the control of a unit and All return the ranges, the line keeps its height, and the tooltips stay inside the chart box. Above the chart of the page Earlier is always light, and Later and Back to the selected range are dim until a window is chosen (Later also while the window ends now) and light after a choice made with the mouse. Above a System chart the strip has no Earlier, Later and Back to the selected range, because the chart shows every value its process has collected, at most 24 hours.
- The Refresh control offers Off, 10 s, 30 s and 1 min: with 30 s the chart and the table are read again every 30 seconds while the window ends now, with Off nothing changes until the button is pressed, the time of the last refresh is written beside the control, and the control is dim for a window that ends earlier.
- The table holds at most 100 PVs and names the limit when a further PV is ticked.
- Value and Last event of a row are the newest sample at or before the end of the window: while the window ends now, the newest sample of the PV; after Earlier, the sample that `getData` returns last for the same window when it is 10 minutes or shorter (a longer window draws a mean in its last bin, which is not a sample).
- The default suite passes, the integration tests that read the page pass (T4), and the book and the Help page describe the pages as shipped: every control they name for the page is on it.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M56: the menu entry and page frame.
- D38: console pages.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- M59: the chart component and its simple form, which the page draws through.
- M62: the analyzer the control opens; the page opens the analyzer as it is until M62 is done.
- M68: the fix of `getDataAtTime` for an instant in the recent past; step 3 reads the Value of a window in the past through it.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the Browse PVs page is a table of the chosen PVs under one chart of at most 5, not a summary; a PV is chosen in the list, drawn by the Plot box of its row, and its less important facts are in the Details window; the owner approved the layout from a clickable mockup.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the chart has one Y axis per unit with its own automatic range, the axes split between the left and the right of the plot, the first half on the left.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: a PV is named in a legend under the chart (line style, name, unit), not by labels at the line ends; a legend item hides and shows its line, the PV keeping its row and its Plot box.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the hover tooltip shows the date and time of the pointer and the value of each plotted PV with its unit.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: with five units the axes are split between the two sides of the plot, and the width left to the plot is not narrowed further; the large window of Enlarge chart is the way to a wider plot.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the tooltip stays as it is, the time of the pointer and the value of each plotted PV with its unit, and does not name the time of the sample a held value comes from.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: Open in the analyzer passes the PVs, the time window and the options the user chose; an option left at its default is not passed and the analyzer applies its own default. Passing the options moved to M62 on 2026-10-15 (see below).
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: a value of a PVA PV that the appliance does not hold is shown as not provided or not set, not as zero.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the plotted PVs and the time window pass to the analyzer in its address, in the parameters the viewer reads today.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: a PV ticked in the list gets its row with the Plot box off; the user turns it on.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the actions on an archived PV (Pause, Resume, Change sampling, Stop archiving, Maintenance) and the cancel of a pending request are in the row of the PV, replacing the Scan list and the Detail area of the Browse PVs page; the owner approved the placement from the mockup.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: Open in the analyzer carries the options chosen on the page as well as the PVs and the time window, so that the analyzer shows the picture the user was looking at; M62 gives the analyzer the parameters to read them. Passing the options moved to M62 on 2026-10-15 (see below).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the Distribution, Two PVs against each other and Summary of the chart panels stay on the Browse PVs page in this item and leave it in M62, when the analyzer carries them, so that no function is lost between the two items (the owner chose this order over taking them off the page here).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the State column is left out while every PV in the table is in its normal state and shown when one is not; the lost events of a row come from the reports `getPVsByDroppedEventsTimestamp`, `getPVsByDroppedEventsBuffer` and `getPVsByDroppedEventsTypeChange`, called without a limit so that each returns every PV that dropped events, and matched by name to the PVs of the table; `getPVDetails` of each row is not used (that call asks the engine, the ETL and the retrieval server and returns about 115 values; it is read when Details opens).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the address keeps `pv` (repeated) for the PVs ticked in the list and gains `plot` (repeated) for the PVs whose Plot box is on; the control into the analyzer is built from `plot`.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the strip above a chart is built in the component of M59 and so is on every chart; it is built in this item because it sits above the chart of the table (the owner chose this item over the analyzer row and a row of its own, and will keep refining it).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: a range is written as an interval, `[a, b]`; a bracket includes the data at that end and a parenthesis leaves it out. The time window of the chart counts the samples at both ends (`p.t >= from && p.t <= to`), so it is written with brackets; a page that leaves the data at an end out passes `fromIncluded` or `toIncluded` false.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the time window is written on a 24 hour clock in the local time of the browser, with the precision of the span (seconds up to 10 minutes, minutes above) and with what both ends share written once in front of the brackets: `2026-10-15 [10:51:45, 11:01:45]` when the hour differs, `2026-10-15 10:[46:50, 56:50]` when the hour is the same too, `[2026-10-14 10:45, 10-15 10:45]` when only the year is the same; the whole interval is the title of the label.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the component draws the strip unless a page passes `strip: false`; the data viewer of the retrieval web application, which has its own bar with the time range and draws one chart for each unit, passes false until the analyzer row decides where the strip of the analyzer goes (the owner chose this over leaving a strip on each of its charts).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the controls of the strip are icons with a tooltip on hover and on focus, not words; a control with nothing to do is dim, not hidden, so that choosing a range moves nothing.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the Std dev column of the table appears only while the standard deviation band of the chart is on, as in the mockup the owner approved.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the bulk actions of today's page stay under the table for the ticked PVs.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the trend of the chosen range that today's Scan list shows beside each PV becomes the Trend column of the table, so that a PV whose Plot box is off can still be seen to move (the owner chose to keep it).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the control of the Browse PVs page passes the PVs and the time window; the options chosen on the page are passed by M62, which defines the parameters of the address and adds them to the control (the owner chose this order over naming the parameters in this item, because the analyzer that reads them is M62's).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: a name the calls do not hold reads "not provided", and a value that is present but says nothing reads "not set": an empty unit, a pair of display, control, warning or alarm limits that are both 0, and a limit that is NaN, for a PVA PV and a CA PV alike (observed on 2026-10-15: the appliance stores no unit for a PVA PV even when the record sets EGU, and its display, warning and alarm limits as 0.0; for a CA PV it stores the unit and NaN for the warning and alarm limits that are not set) (the owner chose this rule on 2026-10-15 over showing the values as received).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the Last event column shows the time of the data of the sample that Value shows, because an event is the event of the signal; the time at which the archiver received the last event is in Details under its own name (the owner chose the time of the data over the time of receipt).
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: Value and Last event are read with `getDataAtTime` for the PVs of the table in one POST, at the end of the time window, so that they move with the window; the parameter `at` is left out while the window ends now, so that the clock of the server decides the present moment; the unit is `meta.EGU` of the answer; a PV without a sample in the search period shows both empty (the owner chose this over the last point of `getData`, which is a bin mean for a window over 10 minutes and has no sample for a window that holds none). A window in the past depends on the fix of `getDataAtTime` that M68 carries.
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: the table asks `getDataAtTime` with `searchPeriod=P30D`; a PV without a sample in 30 days shows Value and Last event empty, with "no sample in 30 days" in the title of the cell (the owner chose 30 days over the default of one day, which hides the last event of a PV silent longer, and over one year).
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: a Refresh control beside the range buttons offers Off, 10 s, 30 s (the default) and 1 min and acts on the whole page, the chart and the table together. Off stops the automatic refresh and a button refreshes once; the time of the last refresh is written beside the control; a window that does not end now is not refreshed and the control is dim; a hidden browser tab pauses the refresh and one refresh follows when it shows again; Value and Last event are read again by one `getDataAtTime` at the chosen period, and the Trend, which needs a `getData` for each PV, is read at most every 30 seconds; the choice is kept in the browser (the owner chose the whole page over the table alone).
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: the Value of an array PV reads `array of N` (N the number of elements), its Last event is the time of the sample, and it has no line in the Trend; the owner chose this over the first element and over a sum or a mean, which read as a value of the signal. What `getDataAtTime` returns for an array PV is written down when the waveform record of the fixture is first archived.
- Open item 2026-10-14 (the owner, from using the Scan list of the page as it is): the State column is empty for a PV that is archived normally, so it reads as missing data. Settled on 2026-10-15 by the decision below. The cleanups made to the Scan list before this item (the Scan heading and the empty lines under the Selected row are gone) end with the replacement of the Scan list and the Detail area by the table.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-15; the owner accepted the plan of eight steps with its criteria and decisions; on 2026-10-16 the owner directed that the strip of a System chart has no time controls and the criterion on the strip and T3 were revised accordingly
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-15; the owner authorized the implementation of the accepted plan, step by step (the owner sees the table of step 3 as a mockup before it is built)
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. Settled with the owner on 2026-10-14: the layout and content of the Browse PVs page and the form of the address (the Decision Date lines above). The order is settled: M59 is built first, because the chart of the page is the simple form of the M59 component, and then this page; M62 follows.
2. The fixtures, first (`src/resources/test/ConsoleChartPVs.db`): the database gains a record whose samples the engine drops: a `calc` with `field(TSE, "-2")` and no source of time, whose time stamp reads undefined (1990-01-01) and falls before the cutoff of the engine, 1991-01-01 (read with the softIoc of EPICS 7.0.10 on 2026-10-15; the report is the check); the same database is served by one `softIocPVX` of the EPICS 7.0.10 installation (`softIocPVX -S -d src/resources/test/ConsoleChartPVs.db`), which serves each record over CA and over PVAccess; a name is archived over one protocol only, so T2 archives `SR:BPM:01:X` and `SR:TICK` through `pva://` and `SR:BPM:02:X` and `FAST:SIG:1` over CA. The dropping record is `SR:DIAG:BADTIME`, archived over CA before the check, the array record is `FAST:WAVE:1`, and the record is built in the working tree (see Progress). Check: `getPVsByDroppedEventsTimestamp` lists the record; a PV is archived through `pva://` and its `getPVTypeInfo` and `getPVDetails` are read to write down which values are absent (observed: the appliance stores no unit for a PVA PV), and the expected result of T2 follows from that reading.
3. Find and the table of PVs (`index.html`, `js/browse.js`, `js/browse/api.js`, `css/browse.css`): the information button and card of the three search modes; a ticked PV adds a row, at most the 100 of today's scan list; the Plot box off by default and at most 5 on, the others disabled with a short reason in their title and the explanation in the information card; the columns Plot, PV, Protocol (the source is `usePVAccess` of `getPVTypeInfo`, `true` for a PVA PV; the name carries no prefix), State (left out while every PV is normal; the lost-events mark taken from the three `getPVsByDroppedEvents*` reports, called without a limit and matched by name), Trend drawn as the Scan list does today, Value aligned on the decimal point with its unit and Last event, both read from `getDataAtTime` at the end of the window (the decision of 2026-10-16), and Std dev (while the band is on); `plot` added to the address; the Refresh control (the decision of 2026-10-16); every element id that `browse.js` uses exists in `index.html` (`scripts/ui-static-checks.bash` collects the ids from `browse.js` and has no list to extend); the marker `<main class="browse">` that three appliance XML tests assert stays, or is changed in them in the same step; the checks that move the window into the past (the Value after Earlier) run after M68 has fixed `getDataAtTime`. Check: T1.
4. The actions (`js/browse.js`): the actions of a row by the state of the PV with the calls of the Browse PVs page (the label Abort the request of today becomes Cancel request), the More menu closing with Esc and a click outside, the window of Stop archiving and Maintenance, and the bulk actions under the table for the ticked PVs. Check: T1.
5. The Details window (`js/browse.js`): the groups of the Scope from `getPVStatus`, `getPVTypeInfo` and `getPVDetails`, each value read by its exact name and shown as "not provided" when the name is absent and as "not set" for a value that is present and empty, a pair of display, control, warning or alarm limits that are both 0 and a limit that is NaN (a PVA PV lacks some, a paused PV has no moves between stores); a time is shown as the call writes it and named by its kind; Esc, Close and a click outside close it and the focus returns to its button. Check: T2.
6. The chart (`js/browse.js`, `index.html`): the component of M59 and its range strip are already on the page (see Progress); this item feeds the chart from the Plot boxes of the table (at most 5), places it above the table, and leaves the Inspect panels (Distribution, Two PVs against each other, Summary of the chart) on the page for M62 to take off. Check: T3.
7. The Open in the analyzer control (`index.html`, `js/browse.js`): the link built from the plotted PVs and the time window; the link Open all selected in the viewer of today becomes Open all selected in the analyzer and goes through `analyzer.html` as this link does. Check: T1.
8. The book (`interface.md`, `operating.md`, the figure of the page), the Browse PVs section of `help.html`, and the tests that read the page: `MgmtPageLinksTest` for the static targets and the three appliance XML tests that assert `<main class="browse">`; the links that the JavaScript of the page builds are read in T1. Check: T4 and T5.

Progress on 2026-10-15 at 10:46 PDT, observed state and not a change of the plan: the range strip is built in `chart.js` and `chart.css`, the Browse PVs page passes it the window, the chosen state, the panning and the information card (the buttons and the note of `index.html` are gone), and the System charts show it without the controls they have no handler for. Observed on a local appliance with real pointer actions: before a choice the three time controls are dim and the window is written as `[from, to]`; a drag over the plot lights them; a drag along an axis lights the control of that unit and writes its range as `[low, high]`; the control of the unit and Back to the selected range return; the strip is 38 px high in every state. Later the same day Earlier was made always active, so that a window can be walked back before any is chosen; Later and Back to the selected range stay dim until a window is chosen. Step 2 observed on 2026-10-15 between 18:58 and 19:12 PDT on a throwaway appliance of the working tree with `softIocPVX` serving the fixture: `getPVsByDroppedEventsTimestamp` lists `SR:DIAG:BADTIME` with `eventsDropped` 1 (the engine counts a repeated time stamp once) while its time of receipt keeps moving; `pva://SR:TICK` and `pva://SR:BPM:01:X` are archived and `getPVTypeInfo` reports `usePVAccess` true, no `units` and no `hostName`, and display, warning and alarm limits 0.0, where the CA PV `SR:BPM:02:X` reports `units` mm, `hostName` and NaN for the warning and alarm limits; a name cannot be archived over CA and PVA together (`pva://SR:BEAM:CURRENT` answered "Already submitted" after the CA request). The rest of the plan is not started.

Progress on 2026-10-16 at 14:26 PDT, observed state and not a change of the plan: steps 3 to 8 are built in the working tree and not committed. Step 3 is the information card of the search modes, the table of PVs (Plot boxes, Protocol, State with the lost-events mark, Trend, Value and Last event from one `getDataAtTime` call, Std dev), the `plot` parameter and the Refresh control (`index.html`, `js/browse.js`, `js/browse/api.js`, `js/browse/format.js`, `css/browse.css`); step 4 the actions of a row, the More menu, the Maintenance window and the bulk actions; step 5 the Details window (`js/browse/details.js`), which replaces the Detail area of the old page; step 6 the chart above the table with the panels below it; step 7 `Open all selected in the analyzer`; step 8 the book (`interface.md`, `operating.md`, `retrieval.md`, four figures), the Browse PVs section of `help.html`, and the range strip text of `comm/css/chart.css` raised to 14 px (the strip of T3 had 12 and 13 px). All checks ran on a fresh local appliance built from the packaged WARs of the working tree (the mgmt WAR holds the files of the source tree), with `softIocPVX` serving `src/resources/test/ConsoleChartPVs.db` and 105 generated records, 13 PVs archived over CA and 2 through `pva://`. Observed beside the plan: (1) the strip above the System charts has the controls of the value axes and Reset all and no Earlier, Later or Back, because those charts show the values their process holds in memory, one point a minute and at most 1440 points, and nothing older is stored; the criterion and T3 name this since the owner's decision of 2026-10-16; the Retrieval performance chart did not exist on the fresh appliance and was not observed; (2) `getPVDetails` has the fields `CAJ channel ID (CID)`, `CAJ server channel ID (SID)` and `CAJ subscription ID`, which the old All details list showed and the Details window does not; the book names the call instead; (3) the call `deletePV` answers one result without PV names for several PVs, so the bulk stop did not remove the stopped PVs from the table or count them; this is fixed in `bulkAction`; (4) a plotted array PV is drawn as the mean of its elements, as before; (5) the unit of a CA record without EGU is returned as an empty string and reads `not set`, and the unit and the host of a PVA PV are absent and read `not provided`; (6) after the consolidation of a PV into the long term store it is paused, its details hold no moves between stores, and its data is in the yearly file of the long term store. A third-person review of the working tree found three items that are fixed: each selection read the three reports of lost events again (30 selections made 90 requests, now 3 within five seconds), an answer for a PV opened earlier could fill the Details window of the next one (reproduced with a delayed answer, then closed by a check that the window still belongs to the PV), and the dialog and the call that archive a PV from the page were unused.

#### M59 - One chart component and its simple form

Origin: daff1b7 / M59
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The Browse PVs page and the viewer share the drawing function `drawTimeSeries` (`staticcontent/js/aa/chart.js`) but not its behavior. Its drawing choices are fixed: a step line (`d3.curveStepAfter`), a circle on each sample only while every PV has at most 200 samples in view (`MARKER_LIMIT`), a linear Y axis (`d3.scaleLinear`) with an automatic range, and, on the Browse PVs page, a bin of the span divided by 600 seconds, so a window of 10 minutes or less shows the stored samples. Pointer handling is written on pointer events: hover shows a crosshair and a tooltip, and dragging selects a window only where the page passes `onZoom`, which only `browse.js` does. The bundled D3 7.9.0 (`d3.min.js`) carries `d3-zoom`, `d3-brush` and `d3-drag`, which are not used.

##### Scope

One chart component. The pages that plot (the Browse PVs page, which hosts the chart in its present form until M58 redesigns it, and the System pages Operations and Retrieval performance) use the same component in a simple form (decision of 2026-10-14, from the Browse PVs mockup): the crosshair and tooltip on hover; a time range chosen by a drag over the plot and a value range by a drag along an axis, a double-click returning; one Y axis per unit, each with its own automatic range; the axes split between the two sides of the plot; a legend under the chart with the line style, name and unit of each PV, an item hiding and showing its line; a hover tooltip with the date and time and the value of each PV with its unit; the Y projection with its mean line and a table of basic statistics of the samples in view (samples, minimum, mean, median, maximum, standard deviation); a Chart options panel with the line (step, straight, smooth, points only), the Y scale (linear, symmetric log, log, square root, a scale that needs positive values falling back to symmetric log with the reason shown), sample marks, a running average and a standard deviation band over a window of samples; an Enlarge chart button that draws the chart again at the size of a large window; and a control that opens their PVs in the analyzer. No other option or analysis tool; the options and gestures it omits are those of the analyzer (M62), which draws through the same component.

Out of scope: the analyzer page, its drawing options, gestures and address (M62); the analysis tools (M63, M64); the page layouts (M57, M58); the explanation of the items of the System pages, their tables and cards (M65); the retrieval server.

##### Completion Criteria

- The Browse PVs page and the System pages Operations and Retrieval performance draw through the component in the simple form, with one axis per unit split between the two sides and a legend under the chart; the Browse PVs page no longer limits its chart to PVs of one unit and has a control that opens its PVs in the analyzer. The Browse PVs page of M58 draws through the component in the same way.
- Each option and gesture of the simple form is observed on archived fixture data; a time range chosen by a drag over the plot issues one batch of data requests after the gesture, one request for each drawn PV and none during the drag, and a value range chosen along an axis issues none.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the controls.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M56: the page frame the component sits in.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- The decisions below on the bundled D3, on the analyzer as a general signal analysis tool and on no external library bind M62, M63 and M64 as well.
- Decision Date 2026-10-12: the Y projection is shown by an option beside the plot, sharing its width; the Distribution panel stays as a separate option.
- Decision Date 2026-10-12: the analyzer is the one place for the detailed options and the analysis tools, including the Distribution panel, the scatter plot and the statistics that the Browse PVs page shows today; the other pages use the component in a simple form with the Y projection only and a control into the viewer. The simple form is widened by the decision of 2026-10-14 below.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the simple form of the other pages carries the options listed in the Scope, from the Browse PVs mockup the owner approved; the Distribution panel, the scatter plot, the full statistics and the other analysis tools stay in the analyzer.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: a chart with PVs of several units draws one Y axis per unit, each with its own range; a PV with no unit shares one axis named no unit.
- Reference of 2026-10-14, read in the browser from the bundled D3 7.9.0 (`js/vendor/d3.min.js`, 578 public names); the component is built from these and the page computes the rest:
  - On a canvas: `d3.line`, `d3.area`, `d3.arc`, `d3.symbol` and `d3.geoPath` take `.context(ctx)`; `d3.contourDensity` gives density outlines, and `d3.Delaunay` and `d3.quadtree` find the point nearest the pointer. The axes (`d3.axis*`) draw SVG only, so a canvas plot draws its ticks from `d3.ticks` and `tickFormat`. Checked by drawing a line, finding a nearest point and drawing outlines on a canvas, and 20000 points drew in 8 ms.
  - Statistics (`d3-array`): `min`, `max`, `extent`, `sum`, `fsum`, `mean`, `median`, `mode`, `variance`, `deviation`, `quantile`, `rank`, `bin` with `thresholdFreedmanDiaconis`, `thresholdScott` and `thresholdSturges`, `bisect` and `bisector`, `group` and `rollup`, `cumsum`, and `blur` for smoothing.
  - Scales, time and format: `scaleLinear`, `scaleLog`, `scaleSqrt`, `scalePow`, `scaleSymlog`, `scaleTime`, `scaleUtc`, `scaleQuantile`; `timeTicks`, `utcTicks` and the time intervals from second to year; `format`, `formatPrefix` (SI prefixes), `precisionFixed`, `precisionRound` and `timeFormat`.
  - Curves and marks: `curveStepAfter`, `curveLinear`, `curveMonotoneX`, `curveCatmullRom`, `curveBasis`, `curveNatural`, `curveBumpX`, and the `symbol` shapes.
  - Interaction: `zoom` (wheel, drag to pan, pinch), `brush`, `brushX` and `brushY`, `drag`, `pointer` and `pointers`, and `transition` with the `ease*` functions.
  - Geometry: `polygonHull`, `polygonArea`, `polygonCentroid` and `polygonContains`; the randomness `randomNormal` and the other `random*` for test data.
  - Not in the bundle, so computed by the page: correlation, covariance, linear regression, the moving average and the exponential average, FFT, a one-dimensional density estimate, and outlier detection.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: every tool of the component uses the implementation of the bundled D3 wherever the bundle has one, and the page writes only what the bundle lacks. The choices: `mean`, `median`, `variance`, `deviation`, `quantile`, `extent` and `fsum` for the statistics; `rank` for the Spearman correlation; `bin` with `thresholdFreedmanDiaconis` for histograms and the Y projection; `scaleDiverging` with `interpolateRdBu` and `scaleBand` for the correlation matrix; `hierarchy` and `cluster` to draw the dendrogram of the clustering; `forceSimulation`, `forceLink`, `forceManyBody` and `forceCenter` for the graph of dependence; `contourDensity` and `Delaunay` for dense scatter plots and the nearest point; `rollup`, `timeHour` and `timeDay` for the pattern by hour and weekday; `scaleTime`, `scaleUtc` and `timeTicks` for the time axis, `format` and `formatPrefix` for values; a canvas `ImageData` with `scaleSequential` and `interpolateViridis`, and `contours` for iso-lines, for an image; `zoom`, `brush`, `drag` and `transition` for the gestures. The page computes only the covariance, the regression and the fits, the principal component analysis (an eigen decomposition of a small matrix), the clustering, the FFT and the autocorrelation.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the analyzer is a general signal analysis tool, not only a tool of accelerator operation; its analyses are those of a general analysis package, and the ROOT manual (histograms, fitting, mathematical libraries, TMVA; read on 2026-10-14) was the reference for the statistics, the profile, the comparison tests, the fit results, the peak search and the mutual information listed in the Scope.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: no external library is added (D40 stays); the least squares, the FFT, the eigen decomposition, the correlation and the tests are written for the page and checked on signals of known parameters.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the options of the chart are one Options panel, opened from the row of the Inspect heading, with the tabs Projection (the histograms at the right edge of the chart and the table of statistics) and Chart (line, Y scale, marks, window, running average and standard deviation band); the Y projection is on while the Projection tab is shown.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the table of statistics and the histograms count the samples inside the time window and, when the viewer dragged a value range out on an axis, inside that range; the running average and the band restart after a gap in the data.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the Enlarge chart window fills the browser window; the table of statistics is in the Projection tab above the chart, on the page and in the window alike.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: charts drawn one above the other (the data viewer) share the width of their widest value axis as well as the room of their labels, so that their plots start at the same place; a chart whose axes and projection would leave its plot under a least width (240 pixels, chosen in the build) is drawn wider than its host, which scrolls sideways inside its own box while the page does not; a sample whose value is not a number is not drawn.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: an axis can take the focus; its arrow keys move its value range, plus and minus narrow and widen it and Home clears it, as the drag along the axis does for the pointer.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: a page says only what changes how the chart reads now (the window shown, the PVs left out); the gestures, the meaning of the values and the options are explained in information cards opened with the i buttons, which link to the help page.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the explanation of the items of the System pages (the tables, the information cards, the state in words, the lines at the top of the Overview) is the milestone M65 and not part of this item; this item keeps what the System charts draw through the component (the legend, its quiet look and the tooltip), and M65 the words of their cards.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the process metric data (`getProcessMetricsDataForAppliance`) returns the UTC epoch of each point, as the book states for the appliance; the zone offset it carried made the axes of the System charts run early by the offset of the host (issue #40).

#### M62 - Analyzer phase A: page, header and address

Origin: daff1b7 / M62
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Not started

##### Summary

The analyzer is the viewer of the retrieval web application (`archViewer.html`, `viewer.js`, `viewer.css`) with few drawing options and no analysis tool. Its menu entry `analyzer.html` forwards to it (`js/analyzer-forward.js`), it carries no site header, logo or menu, and it reads only `pv`, `from` and `to` from its address. The Browse PVs page of M58 opens it and the chart component of M59 draws the simple form; this phase gives the analyzer the site header, logo, menu and time zone choice of the console while it stays an independent service, the page composition the owner approves, and an address that carries the options of the page that opened it; the gestures and options beyond the simple form are phase B (M81) and the analysis tabs are phases C to E. Its input for plotting an archived PV, **Add**, can be taken for starting archiving.

##### Scope

Phase A of `docs/design-analyzer.md` (D46): the analyzer as a page of the console's family, with nothing of the analysis yet.

- The page composition, decided from a clickable mockup the owner reviews: the selection and the range strip at the top, tabs by kind of analysis in the middle (Trend, Distribution, Correlation, Dependency, Spectrum, Compare, Waveform, Image; a tab is enabled by the kind of the chosen signals), a drawer with the tabs Signals, Axes, Options, Data and Export, and the place of the range strip and the options (design, Page composition).
- The independent service with the header of the console: the site header and logo, the same menu as the console pages whose items navigate to the console pages at `mgmtURL`, the time zone choice of M67 (its step 5 moves here), the Analyzer entry marked on both sides; the retrieval `BPLServlet` registers the management's `GetApplianceInfo` action so the page reads `mgmtURL` from its own origin; the marker blocks of the header on the page and the static check covering it; the input for plotting a PV named for what it does (design, Page and header; decisions D1, D2, D6).
- The Trend tab drawn through the chart component in the simple form, with the drawer's Signals, Axes and Options tabs holding what the component has (one axis per unit, the legend, the Chart options), the Data tab with the table of statistics the component has, and the Export tab with Copy link and the CSV of the viewer as they are; the viewer's one chart per unit becomes the split option of phase B.
- The address: `pv`, `from`, `to`, `tz`, `view` (the tab), and the options the component has (`shape`, `yscale`, `marks`, `avg`, `band`, `window`, `yproj`, `yrange`), read on opening, written back as the page changes, unknown names and unreadable values ignored; the control of the Browse PVs page adds the options chosen on the page to the address it opens (design, Address; decisions of 2026-10-14 and D3).
- The book: `interface.md` and `operating.md` for the page as it is after this phase; `MgmtPageLinksTest` for the page and the entry.

Out of scope: the gestures and options beyond the simple form, the Data table of samples and the full Export tab (M81, phase B); the analysis tabs (M63, M82, M64); the Browse PVs panels, which stay (D4 of the design).

##### Completion Criteria

- The analyzer opens from its menu entry and from the Browse PVs page with the site header, logo, menu and time zone choice above it; each menu item opens its console page; the Analyzer entry is marked; the address of the viewer opens on its own.
- No analyzer control uses the wording of archiving a PV.
- The page shows the composition the owner approved: the tabs by kind of analysis with the Trend tab live and the others present but empty or disabled by the kind of signal, and the drawer with its five tabs.
- The Browse PVs page with options set opens the analyzer with the same PVs, window, zone and options; an address with `pv`, `from` and `to` alone opens as before; a name the page does not know or a value it cannot read is ignored; the address follows every change of the page.
- The static check covers the analyzer page's marker blocks; the default suite passes; the book describes the page as shipped.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M59: the chart component and its simple form, which the analyzer extends.
- M58: the Browse PVs page and its control that opens the analyzer.
- D38: console pages.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- The decisions of M59 on the bundled D3, on the analyzer as a general signal analysis tool and on no external library bind this work as well.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the analyzer is an independent service, an application of its own that may be split out of the appliance in the long term, and it carries the same header as the console (logo, menu, time zone choice); the menu items are links that navigate to the console pages at the address of the console, and the analyzer is not shown in a frame of a console page (the owner chose this over the frame of 2026-10-14, which it replaces).
- Decision Date 2026-10-14, replaced on 2026-10-15 by the decision above: the analyzer is shown inside a console page in a frame (the console's content security policy gains `frame-src`; the retrieval web application sets no frame-blocking header), so that the site header, logo and menu are not copied into the retrieval web application; the viewer keeps working on its own address for its own window. The frame is sized by CSS to the window below the header, without `postMessage`. The two origins share only the address.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the options pass as one named parameter per option in the query string of the analyzer's address (`?`, where the viewer reads `pv`, `from` and `to` today), so that an address can be read and edited by hand; M62 lists the names.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: Open in the analyzer passes the PVs, the time window and the options the user chose; an option left at its default is not passed and the analyzer applies its own default.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: Open in the analyzer carries the options chosen on the page as well as the PVs and the time window, so that the analyzer shows the picture the user was looking at; M62 gives the analyzer the parameters to read them.
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the data viewer passes `strip: false` to the chart component, which draws a range strip above every chart otherwise; this item decides where the strip of the analyzer goes (one for the stack of charts, or one for each).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the Distribution, scatter plot and summary panels leave the Browse PVs page in this item, when the analyzer carries them (they stay on the page in M58).
- Decision Date 2026-10-15: the control of the Browse PVs page, which M58 builds with the PVs and the time window, gets the options added by this item, so the parameters are named where they are read.
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the analyzer reads, from its address, the PVs, the time window and the options of the simple form (line, Y scale, sample marks, running average, standard deviation band and its window, the Y projection, and the range of each axis), so that the control into the analyzer of the other pages opens the same picture; an option the user did not set is not in the address and the analyzer applies its own default; each option is one named parameter in the query string, a name it does not know or a value it cannot read is ignored so that an address with `pv`, `from` and `to` alone opens as before, and the range of an axis is given by the unit of the axis (`none` for a PV with no unit); the names and form of the parameters are settled in this milestone.
- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): the analyzer is built in five phases; this row is phase A, planned from `docs/design-analyzer.md`, whose decisions D1 to D6 of 2026-10-19 bind it (the independent service with the console's menu, `getApplianceInfo` on the retrieval, the defaults of the options, the Browse PVs panels staying, the time axis as drawn, the menu that navigates to the other side).
- M67 step 5 (the header of the analyzer with the time zone box and the hand-over of `tz`) is done here.

#### M81 - Analyzer phase B: interaction, options and export

Origin: daff1b7 / M81
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Not started

##### Summary

Phase B of `docs/design-analyzer.md` (D46): the gestures and options the reference tools offer beyond the simple form, and the Data and Export tabs in full, on the page of phase A.

##### Scope

- Gestures (design, Drawing options and gestures; Reference tools): the drag tool chosen on the range strip (select, pan, box zoom), the wheel and the trackpad pinch zooming the time axis around the pointer within limits, Shift and a drag panning, undo and redo of the range, a double-click back, one finger selecting and two fingers panning and zooming on a touch screen, a click on a legend item hiding its line, a click on a series bringing it to the front, a click on a sample pinning its values, two reference cursors with the difference of time and value, the nearest sample found with `d3-delaunay` or `d3-quadtree`, one batch of data requests after a gesture.
- Options (design, Reference tools, Options the tools offer): line width and style, a gap threshold that disconnects the line, a fill between two signals, soft and fixed axis ranges typed per unit, grid lines, centered zero, SI prefixes, an axis label, the averaging interval in seconds or raw samples forced, the min-max band from the retrieval `min` and `max` operators with the mean, a split by unit (one plot per unit sharing the time axis), the legend in table mode with computed values, the tooltip in single or all mode with a sort order, decimals and a display name per signal, transitions on range changes.
- The Data tab: the table of the samples in view with their time, value, severity and status, and the statistics table of the component.
- The Export tab (design, Export): the range (shown or typed), the source (the samples shown, the raw samples, N bins with minimum, mean and maximum, a linear interpolation), the format (wide or long CSV, severity and status, digits, ISO 8601 in the zone or UNIX milliseconds, the unit in the header), the products (data CSV, statistics CSV, plot as PNG or SVG, the address copied), and the retrieval's own `getData.csv` and `getData.mat` addresses for large ranges.
- The address names of every new option, read and written as in phase A; the book.

Out of scope: the analysis tabs (M63, M82, M64); the Browse PVs page.

##### Completion Criteria

- Each gesture and option of the Scope is observed on archived fixture data with mouse, keyboard and touch, and a range change reads the data once after the gesture ends.
- The Data tab lists the samples in view and the Export tab produces each product of the Scope; a CSV of N bins carries minimum, mean and maximum per bin; the exported values equal the retrieval's for the same range and operator.
- Every option is in the address, and an address with the options of phase A alone opens as before.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the controls.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M62: the page, the drawer and the address of phase A.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): phase B of the analyzer, planned from `docs/design-analyzer.md`.
- Open in the design document: the assignment of the drag (the reference tools choose the drag tool on a toolbar with the wheel and hover always on), the labels at the line ends (the legend names the lines), and whether the running average and the band share one window (`window`); each is settled before this plan is accepted.
