#### M63 - Analyzer phase C: tools for one signal

Origin: daff1b7 / M63
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Not started

##### Summary

The Browse PVs page shows a distribution, a scatter plot of two PVs and a statistics table for the PVs of one chart (`plots.js`), and the viewer none. The scatter plot pairs only samples at exactly equal times, so raw samples of two records rarely pair, and it offers only a PV of the same unit at a fixed 150 px height. The bundled D3 has no correlation, regression, fit, FFT or principal component analysis. The analysis of one numeric signal and the comparison of two ranges are built in this phase on the page of phases A and B (M62, M81), from what the D3 bundle provides and from routines the page writes; two and several signals are phase D (M82).

##### Scope

Phase C of `docs/design-analyzer.md` (D46): the tools of one numeric signal and the comparison of two ranges, in the Distribution, Compare and Spectrum tabs of the page of phases A and B (design, Tools by kind of signal; Analysis functions).

- Distribution tab: the summary (samples, minimum, maximum, mean, median, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, the errors of the mean and of the standard deviation, quantiles, lost events); the histogram with the `bin` threshold rules, the box plot, a kernel density estimate; the statistics box and, when a fit of phase D exists, the fit box; the pattern by hour and weekday (`rollup`) and a time-value heatmap for a long span; the values beyond k standard deviations.
- Trend tab additions: the variation (running average, standard deviation band, rate of change), a slow trend (a linear fit against time), the limits of the PV (display, warning and alarm) as reference lines with the time outside them, a threshold line typed by the user with the time beyond it.
- Compare tab: two time ranges of one signal, or two signals, side by side with their ranges linked, the distributions drawn over one another and normalised, the difference of the means and of the spreads, and the tests (chi-square, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling).
- Spectrum tab: the FFT after resampling to an even interval (radix 2 with zero padding, or Bluestein), the window functions, the power spectral density, the peak frequency with its width, the spectrogram over time, the autocorrelation; the sampling frequency typed or read from a companion PV for a waveform.
- The routines the page writes for these: moments, moving statistics, the tests, the FFT, the kernel density estimate; each checked on signals of known parameters made with the `random*` generators.
- The address names of the tabs' options; the fixture records the checks need (a signal with a known distribution and a known period); the book.

Out of scope: two and several signals, fits, derived signals (M82); waveforms and images (M64); state and string signals (after the numeric tools).

##### Completion Criteria

- Each tool of the Scope is available in its tab and is observed on archived fixture data.
- The moments, the tests, the spectrum peak and the autocorrelation return the known parameters of a signal made for the check within the stated tolerance; a time series is resampled to an even interval before an FFT.
- The Compare tab shows two ranges with their ranges linked and reports the tests with their statistics.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the tools.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M81: the page with its gestures, options, Data and Export tabs, which the tools extend.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- The decisions of M59 on the bundled D3 (its functions are used wherever it has one), on the analyzer as a general signal analysis tool, and on no external library bind this work; the page writes only what the bundle lacks.
- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): phase C of the analyzer, planned from `docs/design-analyzer.md`; the tools of two and several signals, the fits and the derived signals are phase D (M82).
- Decision Date 2026-10-14: the tools are added by the kind of signal; the page decides the kind from the type information and the user chooses the purpose within it.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Acceptance: none
Implementation Authorization: none
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. The routines the page writes (new modules under `staticcontent/js/aa/`): moments and their errors, moving statistics, the kernel density estimate, the tests, the resampling and the FFT with its windows, the autocorrelation; each with a unit check on generated signals. Check: T2.
2. The Distribution tab and the Trend additions through the component and the D3 functions of the decision of M59. Check: T1.
3. The Compare tab as a split view with linked ranges. Check: T1.
4. The Spectrum tab. Check: T1, T2.
5. The fixture records, the address names and the book. Check: T3, T4.

#### M82 - Analyzer phase D: tools for two and several signals

Origin: daff1b7 / M82
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Not started

##### Summary

Phase D of `docs/design-analyzer.md` (D46): the tools of two and of several numeric signals, the fits and the derived signals, in the Correlation and Dependency tabs of the page of phases A to C (design, Tools by kind of signal; Analysis functions).

##### Scope

- Correlation tab: a scatter plot of two signals with each axis in its own unit, the samples paired by the value each holds at the other's sample times (`bisector`), with the number of pairs and of samples of the slower signal; the correlation (Pearson, Spearman through `rank`, a cross-correlation over a lag); a profile (the mean of Y with its error in each bin of X); the fit panel after the reference tools: a model chosen (line, polynomial, exponential, power, logarithm, sine, Gaussian, Landau) or typed, initial values, fixed and bounded parameters, a range by sliders, the parameters with their errors, the chi-square per degree of freedom, R², a confidence band, the residuals, earlier fits kept in a list; X and Y projections beside the axes; point size and transparency, points coloured by time, a density contour (`contourDensity`) for dense data, a rectangle brush; the two trends under one another sharing the time axis; derived signals (difference, sum, ratio, one divided by the other).
- Dependency tab, for three to twenty signals averaged over one common interval: the mutual information of each pair and a ranking by how much each explains the chosen one; a correlation matrix as a heatmap ordered by hierarchical clustering with its dendrogram; a scatter plot matrix; the partial correlation; a multiple linear regression with each coefficient, its standardised size, R² and the residuals; a principal component analysis with the variance of each component; a graph of dependence (`forceSimulation`).
- General functions: a derived signal from a typed expression parsed by the page, a change of unit, the export of a fit, a statistics table and a derived signal through the Export tab.
- The routines the page writes: least squares and an iterative least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt) with fixed and bounded parameters, the covariance of the parameters, correlation and partial correlation, mutual information, a small matrix module (multiply, invert, solve, Cholesky, Jacobi eigen decomposition), hierarchical clustering, the expression parser; each checked on signals of known parameters.
- The address names of the tabs' options and the book.

Out of scope: one signal and the comparison (M63); waveforms and images (M64); a vendored library for LOESS or a non-linear fit, and a typed formula as a fit model beyond the expression parser (open items of M63's decisions, settled before this plan is accepted).

##### Completion Criteria

- Each tool of the Scope is available in its tab and is observed on archived fixture data; a pair of different rates shows the number of pairs and of samples of the slower signal.
- A fit of each model, a correlation, a regression and a principal component analysis return the known parameters of signals made for the check within the stated tolerance; the fit panel fixes and bounds a parameter.
- The Dependency tab takes up to twenty signals; the matrix is symmetric with ones on its diagonal and its order follows the clustering.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the tools.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M63: the tools of one signal and the routines it writes (moments, tests, FFT), which the fits and the dependency tools use.
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3; no regression package is added (`d3-regression` is outside the official D3 repositories).
- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): phase D of the analyzer, planned from `docs/design-analyzer.md`.
- Decision Date 2026-10-12: the correlation and the linear regression are computed by the page; the bundled D3 has neither.

#### M64 - Analyzer phase E: waveform and image analysis

Origin: daff1b7 / M64
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #39 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/39)
Status: Not started

##### Summary

The appliance stores an array PV as a waveform (`DBR_WAVEFORM_*`, or `DBR_V4_GENERIC_BYTES` for a PVA structure); it holds no image size, and the data viewer draws a waveform as a time series of its elements. The camera IOC of the site serves row and column profiles of 1920 and 1200 elements, time-series arrays of 2048 points, a histogram of 256 bins and the statistics of up to four regions of interest, and a frame of 1920 by 1200 sixteen-bit pixels at up to 50 Hz. The analysis of arrays and images is built in this phase on the page of phases A and B (M62, M81) and on the tools of phases C and D (M63, M82).

##### Scope

The analysis of waveforms and images in the analyzer.

- One waveform (an array PV): the array at a time, X as the element number or from a companion axis PV; several times overlaid, and the time against the element number as a heatmap; summary values of each array (maximum and its position, minimum, mean, RMS, sum, centre, FWHM) and their time series; the difference from a reference time; the spectrum by FFT with the sampling frequency given by the user or a companion PV, a window function and the peak frequency; a peak search with the position, height and width of each peak, and a background estimated and subtracted.
- An image (a waveform whose element count is width times height, the size given by the user or companion PVs): one frame as a heatmap on a canvas with a colour scale and iso-lines; a rectangle of interest chosen with the mouse; the X and Y projections; the centroid, the peak position, the total intensity and the size by a Gaussian fit in each direction; those values as time series; a background subtraction and the difference of two frames.
- Settled on 2026-10-14 on the recommendation the owner accepted:
  - A waveform: the X axis is the element number, or the array of a companion axis PV when the user names one; the length and the rate are read from `getPVTypeInfo` (the element count and the event rate). The camera IOC of the site, read for this plan, serves row and column profiles of 1920 and 1200 elements, time-series arrays of 2048 points, a histogram of 256 bins and the statistics of up to four regions of interest, so the analysis is built for arrays of that size first.
  - An image: the width and the height come from the companion PVs of the same array plugin (`ArraySize0_RBV` and `ArraySize1_RBV`, with `NDimensions_RBV`, `DataType_RBV` and `ColorMode_RBV`), and the user types them when those are not archived. The camera IOC of the site serves a frame of 1920 by 1200 sixteen-bit pixels (2304000 elements) at up to 50 Hz, so the archived data is expected to be the regional statistics and profiles, and a whole frame is read one at a time.

Out of scope: the page, drawing options and address of the analyzer (M62); the tools for numeric signals (M63); what the site archives of a camera, which the settings of the archiver decide.

##### Completion Criteria

- A waveform is drawn at a time, overlaid and as a heatmap over time; its summary values, their time series, its difference from a reference time and its spectrum are shown.
- An image of a known size is drawn as a heatmap with a colour scale, its region of interest chosen with the mouse, its projections and its centroid, peak, total and Gaussian size computed, and a frame is read one at a time.
- The values agree with the same arrays computed outside the page.
- The default suite passes and the book describes the tools.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M82 and M63: the numeric tools (fits, FFT, statistics) that arrays and images use.
- M62 and M81: the analyzer page, its gestures, options and address.
- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): phase E of the analyzer, planned from `docs/design-analyzer.md` (Waveforms and images).
- D40: the analyzer as a self-contained analysis tool built with the bundled D3.
- The decisions of M59 on the bundled D3, on the analyzer as a general signal analysis tool and on no external library bind this work; a frame is drawn on a canvas with the D3 colour scales and `contours`, the axes and text staying SVG.
- The retrieval response for an array PV and the size limit of one response are read on the fixture before the page is built.

#### M60 - Name check on the network and hold of a pending request

Origin: daff1b7 / M60
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #38 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/38)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

No call tells whether a PV name answers on the control system network before it is archived: the mgmt and engine calls cover only archived or requested PVs (`GetLatestMetaDataAction`, for one, reads only the engine's own channels). CA and PVA search complete names only, so suggestions while typing would need a name service such as ChannelFinder, but a short search for one complete name from the appliance can report its type and server address or that it was not found. A pending archive request can only be cancelled (`abortArchivingPV`): pause and resume act on a PV with a `PVTypeInfo`, which a pending request does not have yet.

Read in the code on 2026-10-18: only the engine can search a name, since the CA and PVA contexts live there (`PVFactory`, the JCA command threads) and the management has none. A request whose name no server answers stays in `METAINFO_GATHERING`: the `MetaGet` of the engine starts its measurement of about a minute only when the channel connects, and the workflow of the management (`MgmtRuntimeState`) aborts the request only after `org.epics.archiverappliance.mgmt.MgmtRuntimeState.abortArchiveRequestInMins`, 24 hours by default, with the reason "user specified timeout"; until then the Archive PVs page reads Initial sampling. An abort reaches the engine as the event `AbortComputeMetaInfo`, which ends the `MetaGet`.

##### Scope

- A call that searches one complete PV name over CA or PVA from the engine of the appliance, with a timeout of 5 seconds by default and a parameter, and answers found with its type and, for a CA name, the host of its server (a PVA channel reports no host), or not found; the management forwards the call to its engine.
- The Archive PVs page searches every name first when Archive is pressed, archives the names that answered, and shows for a name that did not answer the answer of the search and a control Archive anyway, for a name whose IOC is not up yet.
- A pending archive request whose name no server answered within 10 minutes (the setting `org.epics.archiverappliance.mgmt.MgmtRuntimeState.holdArchiveRequestInMins`, named like the abort setting beside it) is held by the appliance itself: its state reads Held with the reason, it leaves the 24-hour abort, and the operator resumes it (the search starts again) or cancels it, from the Archive PVs page, the Browse PVs page and the calls. The hold is a state in memory: archive requests are persisted and restarted from persistence after a restart of the management, so a held request searches again after a restart and is held again ten minutes later; this is accepted, and the hold is not persisted.

Out of scope: suggestions while typing; a name service; a manual hold of a request that is still searching (the appliance holds it after 10 minutes).

##### Completion Criteria

- For a name the IOC of D44 serves over CA the call answers found with the type and the host, for one it serves over PVA found with the type; for a name no server answers, it answers not found within its timeout, 5 seconds by default; the Archive PVs page archives the names that answered and shows, for the others, not found with Archive anyway.
- A request whose name no server answered within the setting reads Held with its reason in `getPVStatus`, on the Archive PVs page and in the State column of Browse PVs, is not aborted after 24 hours, and can be resumed (the search starts again and a name that answers by then is archived) or cancelled.
- Integration tests on the real engine and the IOC of D44 cover the search and the hold; the browser checks cover the page; the default suite and the workflows pass; the book describes the search, the hold and the setting.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M57: the Archive PVs page that uses both.
- D44: the one IOC and the one appliance the checks run on.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The hold is automatic: a request whose name no server answered within 10 minutes is held by the appliance, with Resume and Cancel for the operator; there is no manual hold of a request still searching. The owner chose this over a manual hold alone, so that no request waits a day as Initial sampling.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The page searches the names when Archive is pressed and offers Archive anyway for a name not found, rather than a separate Check names control.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The search waits 5 seconds by default, a parameter of the call.
- Settled by the code, not a choice: the engine runs the search, and the hold is a state of the workflow of the management, since the engine's pause and resume need a channel and a `PVTypeInfo`.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The third-person review of the plan found five things, all applied: the hold time reaches the kept appliance through a new option of the launcher, since the launcher rewrites the properties at every start; the integration test of the hold uses a properties file of its own through the override `TomcatSetup` carries; the time alone decides the hold; `GetPVStatusAction` reads the state from `MgmtRuntimeState`; the hold is not persisted and a held request searches again after a restart of the management.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The second third-person review found three more, applied: a PVA search answers no host; the hold setting carries its full key; the test of the hold clears its system property in its teardown.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The third third-person review found one more, applied: the hold setting is named `holdArchiveRequestInMins`, after its neighbor `abortArchiveRequestInMins`.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The fourth third-person review, a full read, found four more, applied: the expected result of T1 names the host for the CA name only; Browse PVs offers Resume for a held request; the hold check runs before the abort check and an abort setting shorter than the hold makes the hold moot; the page shows the count of names searched and disables Archive meanwhile. The issue body is rewritten at landing. The fifth review found one more, applied: `configuration.md` gains the abort setting beside the hold setting, since the book did not describe it. The sixth review found two more, applied: the timeout of the search is capped at 30 seconds; both settings are read when the management starts, which the book says. The seventh review found one more, applied: on the Archive PVs page Held gets the controls of a pending request but not its fast re-read. The eighth review found one more, applied: the never-connected report carries the state and the reason of a held request, since the meta gets report no longer lists it. The ninth review found one more, applied: at the moment of the hold the workflow reads the meta gets report once and skips a request whose channel connected within the last minute; step 2 is written in three sentences. The second-person pass found six things a next session would have to decide, applied: the fields of the search answer, the forwarding precedent and the registries, the sentences of the reason and of a name not found, the fixture names, the unit test and its assertions, and the restart procedure of the kept appliance.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-18: the owner accepted the plan after nine third-person reviews and two second-person passes of the same day, all findings applied (the automatic hold at ten minutes with Resume and Cancel, the search on Archive with Archive anyway, the five-second search capped at thirty, the launcher option and the per-test properties file for the checks, the fields, sentences, fixtures and tests the plan names)
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-18: the owner authorized the implementation of the accepted plan ("수락과 구현승인")
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. The search: an engine action `searchPV` (`pv`, `timeout` in seconds, 5 by default and at most 30, a larger value cut to 30, since the search holds a servlet thread of the engine for that long) that creates the channel over CA or PVA as `archivePV` chooses the protocol, waits for the connection up to the timeout, answers one JSON object with `pvName`, `found` (true or false), `type` (the `ArchDBRTypes` name, found only), `host` (found over CA only: `EPICS_V4_PV` sets no host), `protocol` (`CA` or `PVA`) and `elapsedMs`, and destroys the channel; registered in `engine/BPLServlet` (`getActions`); a management action of the same name, registered with `addAction` in `mgmt/BPLServlet`, that forwards to the engine of this appliance as `MetaGetsAction` does (`GetUrlContent` on `info.getEngineURL()`); both carry `@BPLEndpoint` for the API reference. Check: T1.
2. The hold. States and transitions: `ArchivePVState` gets a state `HELD` with a reason, the sentence the pages show, `No server answered in <n> minutes` with the setting in effect; the workflow of `MgmtRuntimeState` moves a request from `METAINFO_GATHERING` to `HELD` once `holdArchiveRequestInMins` have passed since the meta information was requested, unless the meta gets report of the engine (`getMetaGetsForThisAppliance`, read once at that moment) shows the `MetaGet` measuring (`isScheduled` true, a channel that connected within the last minute), in which case the tick skips it; the hold ends the `MetaGet` with the abort event; `resumeArchiveRequest` (`pv`), registered with `addAction` in `mgmt/BPLServlet` and carrying `@BPLEndpoint`, puts a held request back to `START`, and `abortArchivingPV` cancels it as before. Settings: `holdArchiveRequestInMins` is 10 by default (its full key is in Scope, a property of `archappl.properties`); a held request is left out of the 24-hour abort, and the hold check runs before the abort check in the same tick, so an abort setting shorter than the hold setting makes the hold moot, which `configuration.md` says beside the two settings. Calls and reports: `MgmtRuntimeState` exposes the state and the reason of a request; `GetPVStatusAction`, which today words every request in the workflow as Initial sampling, reads Held with the reason from it; the never-connected report (`getNeverConnectedPVsForThisAppliance`, which lists the requests of the workflow with their request time, and is where a held request stays once its `MetaGet` is gone from the meta gets report) carries the state and the reason in its rows (`status` and `reason`), and the note of the Show list of Browse PVs for that report reads "Beside each PV: when its archive request was made, and Held with its reason". Check: T1.
3. The Archive PVs page (`js/archive.js`, `archive.html`): on Archive, the search of every name in parallel (at most six at a time), with the count of names searched so far shown and the Archive control disabled until the searches end (tens of names take tens of seconds at the timeout), the archive of the names found, the row of a name not found with the answer of the search, `No server answered in <timeout> s`, and the control Archive anyway, which submits the ordinary archive request for that name; the state Held with its reason and the controls Resume and Cancel (Held joins the states that get the controls of a pending request, not the set the page re-reads at the fast interval, since a held request changes only when the operator acts); on Browse PVs (`js/browse.js`) the State column names the state and the row of a held request offers Resume beside Cancel request; the cards of both pages name the state. Check: T2.
4. The book: `interface.md` and `operating.md` (what happens to a name no server answers, the search, the hold), `configuration.md` (the hold setting and, beside it, the abort setting `abortArchiveRequestInMins`, which the book does not describe yet, with the rule that an abort shorter than the hold makes the hold moot, and the note that both are read when the management starts, so a change needs a restart of the management), the glossary (held); the Help page. Check: T3.

Found on the way and corrected in step 3: `archivePVs` of `js/browse/api.js` had been removed in d17b269e (M58, 2026-10-16), so the Archive button of the shipped page filed no request since then; the restored function is the one of d4c46724.

5. The tests: an integration test of the search (found over CA, found over PVA, not found within the timeout) and of the hold on the real engine and the IOC of D44, the test of the hold starting its Tomcat with a properties file of its own that sets the hold to one minute, through the override of the properties file name that `TomcatSetup` already carries (the system property set before the setup of the test and cleared in its teardown), so that the shared test properties and the other integration tests stay as they are; a unit test `HoldArchiveRequestStateTest` of the state machine over `ConfigServiceForTests` (a request in `METAINFO_GATHERING` moves to `HELD` once the setting has passed, stays when the meta gets report says the channel is measuring, returns to `START` on the resume, and is not aborted by the abort check); `scripts/run-local-appliance.bash` gains an option `--property key=value` that writes the line into the `archappl.properties` it generates at each start, since the generated file is rewritten from the WAR at every start; `work/exp/m58/t_m60_archive.py` on the one appliance of D44, restarted with the hold set to one minute through that option (the restart of the kept appliance follows the book, `developer.md`, "Run a local appliance", with the launcher command of D44: stop the launcher by its pid file, start it again with `--war-dir`, `--port-base 27665` and the run folder, and wait for `getApplianceInfo`). #### M65 - Information cards answer on every page

Origin: daff1b7 / M65
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The four System pages of the console (System, `system.html`; Operations, `operations.html`; Retrieval performance, `retrieval.html`; External servers, `external.html`) are the status monitoring of D38. A table row shows a value, a mark and a word of status; the rules that judge a measure and their threshold values are in `js/system/judge.js` (`THRESHOLDS`). A reader who does not already know the appliance cannot tell from a row what the item is, when its value is normal and what a mark asks for, and a line at the top of the Overview can read Normal while a measure under it is not reported.

The review of 2026-10-17 read the 26 information cards of the console (Browse PVs 2, the chart widget 3, Archive PVs 1, the Overview 9, Operations 7, Retrieval performance 3 and the heap and floor card that Operations and Retrieval share) as a reader who does not know the appliance, and found that the same faults are on every page and not only on the System pages:

1. Cards are missing where a reader is most puzzled. The State column of the table of Browse PVs shows `N lost`, and no card says what it counts or what to do; the columns Protocol, Trend, Value and Last event have none either. M73 showed the cases that such a card has to cover: a type change drops every sample of the new type, and the way out, the change of type in the Maintenance window, works from a number to a number and fails with HTTP 500 for a string or a waveform.
2. Some text is not true to what the appliance does. The Overview card Samples dropped names "a new archive request" as the remedy of a type change, and a request for an archived PV is left as it is. The Operations card Samples lost holds no definition, no list of the three causes and no remedy for any of them; the definition is only in the Overview card.
3. The rows are named in four ways. The Overview cards use What it is, Normal when, Attention when, A problem when and Then; the Operations cards leave out the first two; the Retrieval cards use Slow is, Not a problem and Not recorded; the cards of Browse PVs, of the widget and of Archive PVs name their rows by topic. The row Then does not say that it holds the next step.
4. Terms are used before they are explained: ETL, short term, medium term and long term store, write period, heap floor, block, policy, and in the Write path card the setting `PVTypeInfo.sampleBufferMarginSeconds` of `archappl.properties`, which belongs to the manual. The manual has no glossary page in `SUMMARY.md`.
5. Some sentences do not read at once: in the range card of the chart, "from the range of the buttons too"; the statistics card does not list its columns; the options card says "few" where the manual says 200, and calls a number of samples "Window". A row such as Where data lives has about 90 words.
6. The pages say sample, and the Details window and the reports say events (`eventsDropped`, "How many events").
7. The Operations cards write the threshold values as typed text (30 and 7 days, 5 and 3 %, 50 %, 70 and 90 %, 30 seconds, one hour), which today equal `THRESHOLDS` and drift when it changes; the Overview cards read them from it.

Kept in content, because they work, and only given the row names of the form: the Measure card of Retrieval performance (a limit in seconds and a size per sample), the examples of the search modes, and the titles that are a question.

##### Scope

Every item of every page of the console is readable by itself through an information card (the `i` control of D38), in one form on all pages:

- The title is a question. The first row, In short, answers it in one sentence. A card is of one of two kinds. A measure card (a row of the Overview, a section of Operations or Retrieval performance, the State column) has the rows What it shows, Normal, Attention, Problem and What to do, in that order; a row is left out when it does not apply, so that a card has six rows or fewer. A control card (the search modes, the prefix buttons, the chart options, the time and value range, the statistics, the heap and floor, the largest users, Archive PVs, the external servers) has one row for each item of the control, named as the control names it, and What to do last when there is a next step. In both kinds a sentence has fewer than 40 words, and a term is explained where it first appears in the card.
- The pages are all the pages of the console that hold content, and all of them get the same form. Read on 2026-10-17, they are:
  - Browse PVs (`index.html`): has cards (Find, how to read the chart); gets a card for the table with a row for each column, among them State with `N lost`, its three causes and what to do about each, and Protocol, Trend, Value and Last event. Added on 2026-10-17 at the owner's request: the prefix buttons of the Find panel, which show the PVs of one prefix when pressed and every PV again when pressed a second time, say so in a title on each button and in the Find card, because the second press reads as a reset and is not explained anywhere.
  - The chart widget (`js/aa/chart/widget.js`), which Browse PVs, Operations and Retrieval performance show: has the range, options and statistics cards; gets them in the form.
  - Archive PVs (`archive.html`): has one card; gets it in the form.
  - System (`system.html`), Operations (`operations.html`), Retrieval performance (`retrieval.html`): have cards in their own forms; get the one form.
  - External servers (`external.html`): has no card; gets cards for the list of servers and for Add a server and Remove.
  - Analyzer (the viewer, `retrieval/staticcontent/viewer/archViewer.html`, reached from the menu entry `analyzer.html`): has no card. M62 replaces this page, and its cards (add a PV, the range buttons, Copy link, Download CSV, the chart) are written in M62 in the form of this item (D43); they are not a step or a criterion of this item.
  - Help (`help.html`): a page of steps that links to the cards; its steps use the same words as the cards.
  - The Details and Maintenance windows of Browse PVs: where they carry standing explanation, it moves into a card.
  - Not in the scope, because they hold no content and only forward the reader: `appliance.html`, `cacompare.html`, `integration.html`, `metrics.html`, `pvdetails.html`, `redirect.html`, `reports.html` and `storage.html`.
- A card says what the appliance does. The remedies of the Samples dropped and Samples lost cards follow the cases observed in M73. The settings of `archappl.properties` and the other site setting names are in the manual and not in a card, with a sentence that names the administrator as the one to ask.
- A card takes a threshold from `THRESHOLDS` and a limit of the page from its constant, and types no number twice.
- The word is sample on every page, except where a field is named by the server (`eventsDropped`) and the card says in one clause that the server calls a sample an event.
- The System pages keep what M65 first held: a state in words (Detail) beside the one-word status, the summary table of the Overview with the columns Item, Now, Status, Detail and Open, a measure that is not reported reads Not reported and is never Normal, in a row and in the three lines at the top of the Overview, where a line is Normal only when every measure it rests on is reported. The pages say only what changes how they read now; the explanations are in the cards (decision of 2026-10-14 recorded in M59).

Out of scope: the analyzer, its page layout, its drawing options and the cards of its controls (M62, D43);

Also out of scope: the drawing of the charts (M59); the judgement rules and their threshold values (`js/system/judge.js` stays as it is); new measures and the appliance status as PVA PVs (M61); the page frame and the menu (M56, M57); the note of the Plot limit and the controls of the Plot boxes (M74); a repair of the behaviors that the cards describe (the issues of M73).

##### Completion Criteria

A check in `scripts/ui-static-checks.bash` reads the card sources of every page of the list and refuses a card whose first row is not In short, a card with more than six rows, a card whose rows Normal, Attention and Problem are out of order, and a card with a row after What to do; a page of the list with a control and no card is named by the check.

- No term of the list in Summary item 4 is used in a card before it is explained there, and no card names a setting of a properties file.

- The summary table of the Overview has the columns Item, Now, Status, Detail and Open, and its three top lines rest only on measures that are reported.
- Operations and Retrieval performance show a state in words beside the one-word status, and a measure that is not reported is never Normal, in a row or in a line at the top of the Overview. External servers has no judged measure (a measure of its own would be M61) and shows no status.
- The comment at the head of `js/system/judge.js` names no decision that the register does not hold.
- The book describes the pages item by item and the default suite passes.

#### M67 - Time zone choice for charts and times

Origin: daff1b7 / M67
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The charts and the time texts of the console write times in the time zone of the browser without naming it, and a time that the server writes as text (Details, reports) is in the time zone of the server with its abbreviation. The archiver stores and returns UTC and has no setting for a time zone (`docs/time-handling.md`), so a reader cannot choose the zone in which times are read; a team across sites reads one chart in several zones.

##### Scope

One choice of time zone, kept in the browser, that decides how every chart and time text is written:

- A selection box in the header of the console, one for all its pages, and one in the header of the analyzer. The items are Browser (the default), UTC, Berkeley (`America/Los_Angeles`), Chicago (`America/Chicago`), NYC (`America/New_York`), Seoul (`Asia/Seoul`) and Berlin (`Europe/Berlin`).
- The chart component writes the axis labels, the tooltip, the range strip and its title in the chosen zone and names the zone in the strip. Browser and UTC use the local and the UTC scales of the bundled D3; the five cities are computed with `Intl`, by the offset in force at each tick and not by a shifted date, so that a change of daylight saving time inside a window falls at its true place.
- The choice is kept in the browser store of each application and passes from the console to the analyzer in the address as `tz` (an IANA identifier or `UTC`); a choice made in the analyzer wins afterwards.

Out of scope: the zone of the server as an item; the time handling fixes of the server found in the review of 2026-10-15; the bar of the time range of the viewer (M62); a list of every zone.

##### Completion Criteria

- The selection box lists the seven items, Browser is the default, and the choice survives a reload and is the same on every page of the console.

#### M68 - Time handling of the server and the time page in the book

Origin: daff1b7 / M68
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #42 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/42), for the fix of `getDataAtTime`; the other fixes have no issue
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The review of the code of 2026-10-15 (`docs/book/src/time-handling.md`, moved from `docs/` by this row, is its result) found that the storage, the partitions and the machine readable responses write UTC consistently, and that the edges do not: `getData.jplot` writes a value that is not JSON (an unquoted `ZonedDateTime` with a region identifier in the zone of the server); the text of a time depends on the locale of the server; `getPreviousPartitionLastSecond` keeps the nanoseconds for the 5, 15 and 30 minute partitions; `getDataAtTime` answers a time without a zone with HTTP 500 where `getData` answers 400; `getStartOfYearInSeconds(short)` throws for a year before 1970; `getDataAtTime` for an instant in the recent past returns an older sample when a longer-term store already holds an older one and a shorter-term store holds the newer samples (it returns from the first store that holds any sample, the longest-term store first); an elapsed time, such as the event rate, is the difference of two readings of the wall clock, so a step of the clock changes it; and the book states that the appliance returns UTC, which these responses do not.

##### Scope

- `getData.jplot` writes each point as `[epoch milliseconds, value]`, valid JSON (`JPlotResponse.java`).
- The text of a time (`TimeUtils.convertToHumanReadableString`) is written with a fixed English locale, so that the name of the month does not follow the locale of the server; the zone stays that of the server and is documented as such.
- `getPreviousPartitionLastSecond` clears the nanoseconds for the 5, 15 and 30 minute partitions as it does for the others (`TimeUtils.java`).
- `getDataAtTime`, `GetEngineDataAction` and the other callers of `convertFromISO8601String` answer a time they cannot read with HTTP 400 and the message of `getData`.
- `getStartOfYearInSeconds(short)` returns the start of a year before 1970 as the `int` overload does.
- `getDataAtTime` returns the newest sample at or before the instant across the stores of the PV: `GetDataAtTime.getDataAtTimeForPVFromStores` searches the shortest-term store first.
- The fallback of `fromString` that cannot be reached on the JDK of the project and the stale comments are corrected (`TimeUtils.java`, `JPlotResponse.java`); `convertToLocalEpochMillis`, which has no caller, is removed.
- Elapsed times are measured with `System.nanoTime`: the stopwatch sites, the elapsed seconds of the event rate and the storage rate (`PVMetrics`, `MetaInfo`, `MetaGet`), and the uptime (`MgmtMetrics`); a time written as a moment keeps the wall clock.
- The book: the page of the times (`docs/book/src/time-handling.md`, moved from `docs` and listed in `SUMMARY.md`), the sentences of `faq.md` and `retrieval.md` about time zones, the keys `server_ioc_drift_seconds` and the cutoff of 1991-01-01 in `configuration.md`, and the two meanings of `lastEvent` and the zone of `isDST` in the pages that describe the calls.

Out of scope: the format and the zone of the times that the consoles write (M67, M65); a time without a zone read by the viewer (M62); a time that the server sends together with its epoch seconds (M70); a setting of the time zone of the server.

##### Completion Criteria

- `getData.jplot` returns a body that a JSON parser accepts and whose points are `[epoch milliseconds, value]`, with the same instants as `getData.json` for the same request.
- `convertToHumanReadableString` writes `Oct/15/2026 14:24:42 PDT` form under a Korean default locale.
- For an input with non-zero nanoseconds the 5, 15 and 30 minute partitions return `...:59` with zero nanoseconds, as the hour partition does.
- `getDataAtTime` and the other callers named in the Scope answer a time without a zone with HTTP 400.
- `getStartOfYearInSeconds` of a short year before 1970 equals the `int` overload.
- With the samples of a PV split between the medium term store (older) and the short term store (newer), `getDataAtTime` for an instant after the first sample of the short term store returns the last sample at or before that instant, and for an instant inside the range of the medium term store it returns the sample of that store.
- The book builds, lists the page of the times, and states no sentence that the appliance returns only UTC.
- No elapsed time is the difference of two readings of `System.currentTimeMillis` in the sources of the Scope, and a time written as a moment is unchanged (T3).
- The event rate of a PV sampled at 1 Hz still reads 1 per second within 1 percent after the change; this checks that the values stay right and is not a proof of the fix (T2).
- The default suite passes.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- `docs/book/src/time-handling.md` (moved from `docs/`): the definitions this work makes the code and the book agree with.
- M67: the time zone choice; this item changes nothing in the consoles.
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: the epoch seconds beside the text of a time are a row of their own (M70), not a step of this item, because they change the answer of public calls (the owner chose a separate row over a step of this item or of M67).
- Decision Date 2026-10-16: an elapsed time is measured with the monotonic clock (`System.nanoTime`) and a time that is written as a moment keeps the wall clock (the owner chose to fix the measurements over leaving them as they are). Of the 70 uses of `System.currentTimeMillis`, the stopwatch sites (`PvaGetPVData`, `DataRetrievalServlet`, `GetEngineDataAction`, `WriterRunnable`, `ETLJob`, `PoorMansProfiler`, `ScannedArchiveChannel`, `Throttle`), the elapsed seconds of the event rate and the storage rate (`PVMetrics`, `MetaInfo`, and the start of the timer that measures them in `MetaGet`), and the uptime of `MgmtMetrics` change; the others write a moment (the times of a connection, of the last event and of the last write, the expiry of a static file, the distant future of `ReshardPV` and `AppendAndAliasPV`, the timing text of `DeletePV`) and stay.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-16; the owner accepted the plan of six steps with its criteria and decisions
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-16; the owner authorized step 1 (the stores of `getDataAtTime`), which the Browse PVs page waits for; 2026-10-18, the owner directed steps 2 to 6 ("진행해" on the entry point that names them); commits, pushes and issue changes need their own authority
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. `GetDataAtTime.java` (`getDataAtTimeForPVFromStores`): the stores are searched from the shortest term to the longest and the search stops at the first store that holds a sample at or before the instant (issue #42); the case of two stores that hold different ranges first, in `GetDataAtTimeForPVFromStoresTest`. Check: T1.
2. `TimeUtils.java`: the nanoseconds of the three minute partitions, the year before 1970, the locale of the text, the fallback and the stale comments, the removal of `convertToLocalEpochMillis`; the tests first in `TimeUtilsTest`. Check: T1.
3. `JPlotResponse.java` and the callers of `convertFromISO8601String` (`GetDataAtTime.java`, `GetEngineDataAction.java`, `SlicePBFile.java`): the response of `jplot` and the answer to a time that cannot be read. Check: T2.
4. The stopwatch sites and the rates (`PvaGetPVData.java`, `DataRetrievalServlet.java`, `GetEngineDataAction.java`, `WriterRunnable.java`, `ETLJob.java`, `PoorMansProfiler.java`, `ScannedArchiveChannel.java`, `Throttle.java`, `PVMetrics.java`, `MetaInfo.java`, `MetaGet.java`, `MgmtMetrics.java`): `System.nanoTime` for the elapsed time, the epoch seconds that are shown unchanged. Check: T2 and T3.
5. The book (`docs/book/src`): the page of the times, `SUMMARY.md`, `faq.md`, `retrieval.md`, `configuration.md`. Check: T3.
6. The default suite and the workflows. Check: T4.

Progress on 2026-10-16 at 01:50 PDT, observed state and not a change of the plan: step 1 is built in the working tree and not committed. `GetDataAtTimeTwoStoresTest` (13 tests) fails on the original order of the stores in 4 of its first 7 tests; `getDataAtTimeForPVFromStores` now searches the shortest-term store first and a store that cannot answer does not stop the search of the next one (searching the shortest-term store first alone made some instants answer nothing, because a short term file that holds only samples later than the instant throws `Max iterations reached`, which is #43). `GetDataAtTime*Test` passes with 26 tests and `./mvnw -B -ntp clean verify` with 977 tests and no failure. On a local appliance of the working tree the instants that answered a sample an hour old or nothing answer the newest sample at or before them (`at` 06:59:59.400Z answers 06:59:59.354Z, where it answered 05:59:59.354Z). A comparison of `getDataAtTime` with the last sample at or before the instant read with `getData`, for 8 PVs at 10 instants, agrees in 79 of 80 cases; the other case is a PV whose newest sample is the only sample of its day file and of its hour file, which the backward reader of a PB file does not return (M71). The rest of the plan is not started.

#### G7 - aa-env installation checks of the MariaDB socket and TCP paths at 61e1b4c5 or later

Origin: daff1b7 / G7
GitHub Issue: #31 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/31)
Status: Complete

#### M40 - Modernize the retained state-changing sample scripts

Origin: daff1b7 / M40
Identity History: split from M37 on 2026-10-04
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Not started

##### Summary

M37 originally held fourteen retained sample scripts. On 2026-10-04 the owner kept the read-only and alert groups in M37 and moved the two groups that change appliance state here: recovery selection (abortNeverConnectedPVs.py, resumePausedPVsMatchingPattern.py) and storage and configuration (consolidatePausedPVs.py, consolidateArchivedData.py, changeArchiveStore.py, addPostProcessingOperator.py, removeMetaFields.py). M37's Summary records their current defects: no timeouts, HTTP 200 taken as success, the unchecked pause, consolidate and resume sequence with an unconditional resume, the full PVTypeInfo post with override=true, and the getAllPVs default limit of 500.

##### Scope

Bring these seven scripts to the contract M37 defines for its scripts (explicit BPL URL, per-request `--timeout`, exit 0, 1 and 2, results on stdout and diagnostics on stderr), reusing M37's shared Bash mechanics, while keeping each script's target selection, request order, side effects and final state explicit. Document each in the scripting page.

Out of scope: the M37 scripts; the eight commands delivered by M17; server corrections, which take their own scope when a script exposes a defect.

##### Completion Criteria

- Each of the seven scripts has a defined input, response, dependency, timeout and failure contract, reports an application-level rejection and an uncertain outcome as such, and does not report success on HTTP 200 alone.
- Each keeps the procedure recorded in M17's function map, and every intentional change from the legacy behavior is named with its reason.
- Each is verified by executing its shipped entry point against the real appliance and the shipped IOC fixture, with the original and the replacement compared on the same fixtures before the original is removed; the scripting page documents each.

- Origin: split from M37 by the owner on 2026-10-04; unassigned until the owner assigns it.
- M37: the language (Bash), the per-request timeout and the shared mechanics come from M37.
- Decisions carried from M37 (Decision Date 2026-10-04): consolidateArchivedData.py checks the result of each step and resumes only the PVs it paused itself; addPostProcessingOperator.py requests getAllPVs with an explicit limit; the three type-info scripts keep posting the complete PVTypeInfo with override=true, add a readback that confirms only the intended field changed, and document that a concurrent change between read and post can be overwritten.
- Constraints carried from the research: the two consolidation scripts end in different states and stay separate procedures; removeMetaFields.py has no internal pause or resume; no automatic retry of a mutation.

#### M70 - Epoch seconds beside the text of a time in the management calls

Origin: daff1b7 / M70
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The management calls write a time as text in the time zone of the server with its abbreviation, such as `Oct/16/2026 01:04:19 PDT`: the 17 time values of `getPVDetails` (each an element with `name`, `source` and `value`), `lastEvent` of `getPVStatus`, `creationTime` of the reports. `TimeUtils.convertToHumanReadableString`, which writes the text, is called from about fifty files; the ones that put a time into the answer of a call include `PVMetrics`, `EPICS_V3_PV`, `EngineChannelStatus`, `ETLMetrics`, `ETLDetails`, `RetrievalMetrics`, `PVDetails` and the reports that write a time (`PausedPVsReport`, `RecentlyAddedPVsforThisInstance`, `NeverConnectedPVsForThisAppliance`). A client cannot write such a time in another time zone, because an abbreviation such as `CST` names several zones and the text holds no offset. The time zone choice of the viewer (M67) needs the same instant as epoch seconds.

##### Scope

Each time that these calls write as text is accompanied by the same instant as epoch seconds (UTC), added as a field beside the text. The existing fields stay as they are, so that a client that ignores an unknown field keeps working.

- `getPVDetails`: an element that holds a time gets `epochSeconds` (an integer); the text `Never` and `N/A` have none.
- `getPVStatus`: `lastEventEpochSeconds` beside `lastEvent`, and the same for the other times of the answer; `PvaGetPVStatus` carries the same.
- The reports that write `creationTime`, `modificationTime` and the like: `<name>EpochSeconds` beside each.

Out of scope: removing or changing the text; the zone of the text, which stays that of the server; the retrieval responses, which carry epoch seconds already; the consoles (M67, M58).

##### Completion Criteria

- Every time value of `getPVDetails` has `epochSeconds` equal to the instant of its text, and an element without a time has none.
- `getPVStatus` and the reports named in the Scope carry the epoch seconds beside each time text.
- A client that reads only the old fields gets the same answer as before: the existing fields and their text are unchanged.
- The book names the new fields and the default suite passes.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- Origin: recorded on 2026-10-16 at the owner's direction as a row of its own, from the open decision of the time review (the owner chose a separate row over a step of M68 or of M67).
- M67 reads these fields to write the times of Details in the chosen zone; M58 shows them as the server writes them until then.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The owner settled the names and the list (step 1). Names: `epochSeconds` as one more key of a time element of `getPVDetails`; `<name>EpochSeconds` beside a time of a flat answer (`lastEventEpochSeconds`, `creationTimeEpochSeconds` and so on). List, read from the 54 callers of `convertToHumanReadableString`: the 17 time elements of `getPVDetails` (`PVMetrics` 7, `EPICS_V3_PV` 2, `MetaGet` 1, `ETLMetrics` 2, `ETLDetails` 2, `RetrievalMetrics` 1, mgmt `PVDetails` 2); the 4 times of `getPVStatus` in `EngineChannelStatus` (`lastEvent`, `lastRotateLogs`, `connectionFirstEstablished`, `connectionLastRestablished`) and the same values of `PvaGetPVStatus`; the reports `PausedPVsReport` (`modificationTime`), `RecentlyAddedPVsforThisInstance` (`creationTime`), `RecentlyChangedPVsforThisInstance` (`modificationTime`), `NeverConnectedPVsForThisAppliance` (`requestTime`, `startOfWorkflow`), `CurrentlyDisconnectedPVsAction` (`lastKnownEvent`, `connectionLostAt`), `SilentPVReport` (`lastKnownEvent`) and `ProcessMetrics` (the start of the process). Left out, because no console reads them: the step timings of `DeletePV` (engine and ETL), `ArchiveChannelObjectDetailsAction` and the sample `ts` of `CompareWithChannelArchiver`.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-18; the owner accepted the names and the list of step 1 ("ㅇㅋ")
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-18; the owner authorized the implementation ("구현승인"); commits, pushes and issue changes need their own authority
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. Settle with the owner the names of the fields and the list of the calls and reports, found by reading every caller of `convertToHumanReadableString` that puts a time into an answer. Done on 2026-10-18 (the decision above).
2. Add the fields in the code that writes each time (the files that step 1 lists), the test first. Closes with T1 and T2.

##### Test Plan

#### M71 - Backward read of a small PB file

Origin: daff1b7 / M71
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #43 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/43)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

A backward read of a small PB file fails in two ways, in two classes.

`ReverseLineByteStream.readLine` tests `chReadUntil + currentBufferPos < stopAtPosition` before it returns the line that the constructor has already buffered. For a file with one sample that line directly follows the header, so the test always holds and the line is never returned. Observed on 2026-10-16 by running the class on files written by the storage plugin, with the start position at the first sample and the end position at the end of the file: 0 lines for a file with one sample, every line for files with two to four samples. The search is not involved: for a one-sample file `FileBackedPBEventStream` replaces a search result of 0 or less by the size of the file (43 bytes in the file tried), and the stream is still empty. The backward reader is used only through `PBEventStreamPositionBasedReverseIterator`, which only `FileBackedPBEventStream` creates.

`FileEventStreamSearch.binarysearch` throws `IOException: Max iterations reached` when it looks in a small PB file for a time that is earlier than every sample of the file, where its callers expect `false`. It happened for the file of an hour partition of the short term store that held only the samples written after an ETL run, through `FileBackedPBEventStream.seekToEndTime` and `PlainPBStoragePlugin.iterate`; `getData` over the same file for the same times succeeded. The throw site is known, and the cause was confirmed on 2026-10-16 by tracing the loop on such a file: when the sought time is earlier than the first line, every step is `GO_LEFT`; once `mid` is `min`, `max` becomes `min - 1`, `(max - min) / 2` is 0 in integer division, so `mid` stays `min`, `min` and `max` do not change, and the loop repeats until the counter of 1000 iterations ends.

Effect on `getDataAtTime`: on 2026-10-16 on the local appliance, `getDataAtTime` for `BL:01:SHUTTER:STATE` at 08:18:19Z and 08:18:36Z answered the sample of the day before, because the sample of 08:18:18.354Z was the only one in the day file of the medium term store and the only sample in the hour file of the short term store was later. The cases that fail are listed under Cases.

##### Scope

Step 1: a backward read of a PB file with one sample, with an end time at or after that sample, returns the sample, and the reads of files with two or more samples return the same lines as before.

Step 2: the search ends with `false` when the sought time is earlier than the first sample of the file, and the loop ends by its interval and not by the counter of iterations, which stays a guard against a corrupt file.

Out of scope: another search algorithm; the choice of the partition files of a time. Considered and left to a later item, because they change the cost and not these defects: computing the name of the partition file of the time instead of listing the folder of the PV (`PlainPBPathNameUtility.getPathsWithData` reads the whole folder at each call), reading the end of the file directly for a time after its last sample, and reading a file of a few kilobytes from its start.

##### Completion Criteria

- `ReverseLineByteStream`, given the start position of the first sample, reads the sample of a file with one sample and returns the same lines as before for files with two or more samples.
- A backward iteration over a PB file with one sample, with an end time equal to or later than the sample, yields that sample, and `getDataAtTime` answers the newest sample at or before the instant when the files of the stores hold one sample each.
- For a PB file with one sample and for a file with two samples, a search for an end time earlier than the first sample returns `false` and throws nothing.
- Searches for times inside the range and after the last sample return the same positions as before.
- The existing search and reverse reader tests and the default suite pass.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- Origin: recorded on 2026-10-16 at the owner's direction, from the observation made while fixing `getDataAtTime` (M68, issue #42), which stops its search of the stores on the exception of step 2 and now continues with the next store. The one-sample case was added on 2026-10-16 at the owner's direction; its first recorded cause (the search) was corrected the same day after the reverse reader was run on the files.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. One item with two ordered steps, the reverse reader first, because both show in the small files of a freshly started store and both close with the same `getDataAtTime` check.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-16; the owner accepted the plan of three steps with its criteria and the decision of one item with two steps
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-16; the owner authorized the three steps of this plan
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. The tests first, then `ReverseLineByteStream.readLine`: in `ReverseLineByteStreamTest` a file written with a header and one line, read with the start position of that line; in the tests of the PlainPB package a backward iteration over a file written by the storage plugin with one sample, with end times before, at and after the sample; in `GetDataAtTimeTwoStoresTest` a PV with one sample in the day file of the medium term store and one in the hour file of the short term store. Each fails on the code before the change. Closes with T1.
2. The tests first, then `FileEventStreamSearch.binarysearch`: in the search tests of the PlainPB package a file written by the storage plugin with one and with two samples, searched for a time before them; the loop is traced on that file before the change to settle the hypothesis of the Summary. Closes with T2.
3. The default suite and the workflows. Closes with T3.

##### Progress

Progress on 2026-10-16 at 08:40 PDT, observed state and not a change of the plan: steps 1 and 2 are built in the working tree and not committed (`ReverseLineByteStream.readLine`: a line already buffered is returned and the stop position applies only to reading a further line; `FileEventStreamSearch.binarysearch`: the loop ends when an iteration leaves `min` and `max` unchanged). On a local appliance built from the working tree, `getDataAtTime` for `BL:01:SHUTTER:STATE` at 08:18:19Z and 08:18:36Z answers the sample of 08:18:18.354Z where it answered the sample of the day before, and the comparison of `getDataAtTime` with the last sample at or before the instant read with `getData`, for 8 PVs at 10 instants, agrees in 80 of 80 cases (79 of 80 before the changes of this detail). The workflows have not run.

##### Cases

Observed on 2026-10-16 by running the tests of this detail on the code before the change and on the working tree, case by case through a temporary harness that calls the same test methods and was not kept. The files are day files written by the storage plugin with the header line of a PB file; the samples are at 60.354 s, 280.354 s and 500.354 s after the start of the day, and the end times are in seconds after the start of the day.

| Case | Before the change | After the change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backward iteration, file of 1 sample, end time before the sample (30 s, 60 s) | Correct: no event at or before the end time | Same |
| Backward iteration, file of 1 sample, end time at or after the sample (61 s, 279 s, 280 s, 500 s, 1120 s) | Wrong: no event is yielded, the sample is missed | Yields the sample |
| Backward iteration, file of 2 or 3 samples, end time before the first sample (30 s, 60 s) | `IOException: Max iterations reached` | No event at or before the end time |
| Backward iteration, file of 2 or 3 samples, end time at or after the first sample (61 s to 1120 s) | Correct | Same |
| `ReverseLineByteStream` from the start position of the first sample to the end of the file, file of 1 line | 0 lines | The line |
| `ReverseLineByteStream`, files of 2, 3 and 4 lines | Every line | Same |
| `getDataAtTime`, one sample in the day file of the medium term store and one later sample in the hour file of the short term store, end times 60.354 s, 61.354 s, 279.354 s, 280.354 s, 290.354 s | The older sample of the previous day (5 of 6 end times tried) | The newest sample at or before the end time |
| `getDataAtTime`, same PV, end time 30 s | Correct | Same |
| `getDataAtTime`, PV with two samples in the hour file, 8 end times | Correct | Same |
| Search with the comparison of `FileEventStreamSearchSmallFileTest`, header line and 1 to 3 lines, number before the first line | `Max iterations reached` for the files with a header (1 to 3 lines) | Not found, no exception |
| Same search, number at or after the first line | Found for the files with a header | Same |
| Same search, files without a header line (a layout that PB files do not have), lines 100, 200, 300 | Files of 2 and 3 lines: `Max iterations reached` for the numbers 50, 100 and 150; file of 1 line: not found for 50, 100 and 150 | Files of 2 and 3 lines: not found for 50, found from 100 on; file of 1 line: not found, as before |

Not tried: files of four or more samples for end times before the first sample (the existing search test on a file of 5000001 lines passes for numbers below the first line).

##### Test Plan

#### M72 - One chart widget with its controls

Origin: daff1b7 / M72
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The chart component of M59 is a drawing function, `drawTimeSeries` in `staticcontent/js/aa/chart.js` (1122 lines), with the parts it draws; each page adds the controls itself. Read on 2026-10-16: `js/browse.js` holds the state of the options (`chartOptions`, `optionsOpen`, `optionsTab`, `projection`), the markup of the Options panel and its tabs, the Enlarge chart window (it moves the chart into a dialog and back), the link into the analyzer, the text of the four information cards of the chart, and the time window with its pan, zoom and return; the pages `js/operations.js` and `js/retrieval.js` pass the series, the window and a few drawing choices (the legend, the gap, whether the lines carry names) and nothing else, so their charts have no Options panel and no Enlarge chart; the data viewer (`retrieval/staticcontent/viewer/viewer.js`) draws one chart for each unit with the range strip turned off. The decision of 2026-10-14 in M59 says that the pages that plot carry the simple form with its options, and the Scope of M59 lists the Options panel and Enlarge chart in it; the completion criteria and step 3 of M59 narrowed the System pages to the legend and the tooltip, and M59 was closed against them. The owner's intent is one component that holds everything and that the pages only place.

Also read on 2026-10-16: the helper `node` is defined in six places, not three (`js/system/api.js`, which three System pages import, `js/archive.js`, `js/browse.js` and `js/browse/details.js` with the same body, and `viewer/viewer.js` and `js/external.js` with a body that does not skip a null child). The first of the four information cards ("Reading the chart") is written for the Browse PVs table (the Plot boxes and the limit of PVs); only the cards of the range, the options and the statistics are generic. The information control and its card (`infoButton` in `js/system/view.js`, `button.info` and `.card` in `css/system.css`) belong to the management folder, which a widget in the shared folder cannot import; the Options CSS (`opt-*`) is already in the shared `css/chart.css`. The pages are all ES modules, and the build serves the whole shared folder as `ui/comm`, so a subfolder `js/aa/chart/` needs no change of the build. Operations and Retrieval performance build their chart host again at a refresh, so options kept in the host element would be lost. `drawTimeSeries` is 523 lines: the geometry and axes, the lines and marks, the Y projection (834 to 876), the direct labels, and the gestures and keys (942 to 1100).

##### Scope

One widget, `createChart(host, config)`, in the shared component (`staticcontent/js/aa/`), that builds and keeps what a chart needs and that every page places.

What the widget holds:

- The row of the chart with the Options button, the Enlarge chart button and the link into the analyzer when the page gives its address.
- The Options panel with the tabs Projection and Chart and the state of the options (line, Y scale, marks, window, running average and band).
- The Enlarge chart window, built by the widget, which closes with Esc and its Close button and returns the focus to its button; it covers the browser window, so there is no backdrop to click.
- The cards of the chart: the range, the options and the statistics, written once with their link to the help page. The first card, how to read this chart, is given by the page, because its text names the controls of the page.
- The range strip, the legend, the tooltip, the Y projection with its statistics and the gestures that `drawTimeSeries` has today.
- A place for the display time zone in the configuration (`config.timeZone`), which M67 fills; this item sets no zone.

The configuration of the widget:

- `config`, given once: `id` (a string; the options and the open tab are kept in the module under it, so a page that builds its host again at each refresh keeps them), `idPrefix` (a prefix for the id of each control, for a page with more than one chart; without it the ids are `optionsToggle`, `enlarge`, `chart` and so on), `title` and `dialogTitle` (the headings of the row and of the large window; optional), `help` (the first card as `[title, rows, action, helpHref]`; optional), `helpHref` (the help page of the cards of the widget), `legend`, `labelNames`, `strip` (default true), `timeZone` (reserved for M67; the widget does not read it) and the optional callbacks `onZoom(from, to)`, `onPan(direction)`, `onReset()` and `onOptionsChange(options)`. The large window is built the first time Enlarge chart is pressed and is left in the page when it closes.
- With no `onZoom` there is no drag over the plot; with no `onPan` and no `onReset` the strip has no Earlier, Later and Back to the selected range, as the System charts have today.
- `draw(data)`, called at each refresh: `series`, `from`, `to`, `gapMs`, `windowChosen`, `canPanLater` and `analyzerHref` (a string, or null for no link). `options` reads the options chosen; Browse PVs reads `band` to show the column of the standard deviation and gives `onOptionsChange` to redraw its table.

The modules. `staticcontent/js/aa/chart.js` stays as the entry that the pages import and exports `createChart`, `drawTimeSeries`, `axisRoom`, `labelRoom` and `CHART_OPTIONS`; its code moves, without a change of behavior, into `staticcontent/js/aa/chart/`:

- `text.js`: `format`, `intervalText`, `windowLabel`, `shortNames`.
- `series.js`: `finiteSeries`, `splitOnGaps`, `movingStats`, `lineLook`, `PALETTE`, `DASHES`.
- `scales.js`: `makeValueScale`, `axisWidthOf`.
- `layout.js`: `labelWidth`, `labelLayout`, `labelRoom`, `axisRoom` (the viewer imports the last two).
- `strip.js`: `stripIcon`, `keepTipInside`, `stripControl`, `buildRangeStrip`.
- `legend.js`: `buildLegend`. `statistics.js`: `buildStatistics`.
- `options.js`: `CHART_OPTIONS` and `buildChartOptions`, the form of the Chart tab.
- `projection.js`: from `drawTimeSeries`, the samples in view of each line, the rows of statistics and the bars and mean line of the Y projection; it takes the SVG, the drawn series, the scales, the ranges, the margins and the axis width as parameters and returns the rows.
- `gestures.js`: from `drawTimeSeries`, the drag across the plot, the drag along an axis, the keys of an axis and the double-click; it takes the SVG, the geometry (`width`, `height`, `margin`, `plotTop`, `plotBottom`, `axisWidth`, `onLeft`, `onRight`, `axisAt`), the time scale, the value scales, the units, the ranges, the callbacks of the page and a `redraw` function.
- `draw.js`: `drawTimeSeries`, which keeps the geometry, the axes, the lines, the marks and the direct labels and assembles the parts above.
- `widget.js`: `createChart`.

Beside them, in `staticcontent/js/aa/`: `dom.js` with the one `node` helper (the version that skips a null or undefined child), which replaces the six definitions, and `card.js` with the information control and its card.

Pages that move onto the widget: the Browse PVs page, which keeps the Distribution panel, the scatter plot and the Summary of the chart for M62, and the System pages Operations and Retrieval performance. The viewer keeps `drawTimeSeries`, `axisRoom` and `labelRoom` through `chart.js` and takes `node` from `dom.js`; Archive and External take `node` from `dom.js` and nothing else changes in them.

Out of scope: the analyzer and its viewer (M62); the words of the information cards of the System pages (M65); the analysis tools (M63, M64); the selection of the time zone (M67); the server calls.

##### Completion Criteria

- A chart of Operations and of Retrieval performance has the Options button with its panel (Line, Y scale, Marks, Window, Running average, Standard deviation band and the Projection tab) and the Enlarge chart button, and no link into the analyzer and no Earlier, Later or Back to the selected range.
- The Browse PVs page behaves as it does at the commit d17b269e of M58: the checks of its T3 (axes and their sides, the strip, the gestures, the Projection tab, the legend, the tooltip, Enlarge chart, the options Line and Y scale) give the same results.
- The options chosen on a chart are kept by the widget, under the `id` of the chart, while the page is open, and survive the refresh that draws the chart again, on the System pages that build their host again as well.
- `staticcontent/js/aa/chart.js` is the entry and its code is in the modules `text`, `series`, `scales`, `layout`, `strip`, `legend`, `statistics`, `options`, `projection`, `gestures`, `draw` and `widget` of `staticcontent/js/aa/chart/`; the pages, `js/browse.js`, `js/operations.js`, `js/retrieval.js` and `viewer.js`, import `chart.js` without a change of what they draw.
- The helper `node` is defined once, in `staticcontent/js/aa/dom.js`; `js/system/api.js`, `js/archive.js`, `js/external.js`, `js/browse.js`, `js/browse/details.js` and `viewer/viewer.js` hold no definition, and the calls of `viewer.js` and `external.js`, whose copies did not skip a null child, are read for a null or undefined child.
- The information control and its card are defined once in the shared folder (`js/aa/card.js`), and the System pages and the Archive page show the same cards as before.
- `js/browse.js` builds no Options panel, no Enlarge chart window, no card of the range, the options or the statistics and no link into the analyzer, and passes its first card as `help`; the controls are created by the widget and the checks of `scripts/ui-static-checks.bash` pass.
- The book and the Help page describe the controls of the charts of the System pages, and the default suite passes.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M59 (Complete): the component and its simple form; this item completes what its decision of 2026-10-14 says and its criteria left out. M59 stays Complete and its record is not changed.
- M58: the Browse PVs page is moved by this item, so the work follows the commit and the verification of M58 (work ordering). The ordering is met: the commits d17b269e, f0b31a72 and a1747759 are on origin/modernize and M58 / T1 to T5 pass; M58 stays In progress only for the closure of its issue.
- D38: explanations open on demand, in cards.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. The owner directed that the chart is one component that contains everything and that the pages place it, and that this is a new item and not a reopening of M59.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. A System chart has no time controls, because its process holds only the last 24 hours in memory, one point a minute, and stores nothing older; this is the decision recorded in M58.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. The owner directed that `chart.js` is split into modules by role and that the repeated DOM helper becomes one shared function, in this item; the plan keeps the split apart from the change of behavior (step 2 and step 3).
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. The options of a chart are kept while the page is open and not in the browser between visits: the right line shape and scale depend on the PVs shown (the log scale needs values above zero), so an old choice would misread the next visit.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. The information control with its card moves into the shared folder (`js/aa/card.js`, `css/chart.css`): the state of the open card and the CSS of `button.info` and `.card` go with it, and `js/system/view.js` and the pages import it from there and keep no copy. The other way, a function given by the page in `config`, was rejected because the viewer in the retrieval web application imports nothing from the management folder and could not show cards.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. The browser checks use one fixed list of the records of `src/resources/test/ConsoleChartPVs.db` (25 records: 20 scalar doubles, the double waveform `FAST:WAVE:1`, the enum `SR:OP:MODE`, the string `SR:OP:MESSAGE`, the integer `SR:INJ:COUNT`, the helper `SR:OP:MODECODE` that is not archived, and `SR:DIAG:BADTIME`, which the engine refuses). Checks that change nothing run on the kept appliance, which archives `SR:TICK`, `SR:BPM:01:X`, `SR:BPM:01:Y`, `SR:BEAM:CURRENT`, `SR:BEAM:LIFETIME`, `SR:RF:CAV1:TEMP`, `SR:RF:CAV1:POWER`, `SR:VAC:01:PRESSURE`, `BL:01:MOTOR:POS`, `BL:01:SHUTTER:STATE`, `SR:DIAG:BADTIME`, `FAST:WAVE:1`, `SR:OP:MODE`, `SR:OP:MESSAGE` and `SR:INJ:COUNT`, so that earlier and present data are read together. Checks that pause, stop, rename, change the type or consolidate run only on a temporary appliance on `SR:BPM:02:X`, `SR:BPM:02:Y`, `SR:BPM:03:X`, `SR:BPM:03:Y`, `SR:BPM:04:X`, `SR:BPM:04:Y`, `SR:RF:CAV2:TEMP`, `SR:RF:CAV2:POWER`, `FAST:SIG:1` and `FAST:SIG:2`, which a check archives or resumes at its start. No other name is added to either appliance; the one exception is the check of the limit of 100 rows, which needs 101 known names and uses 105 generated names on the temporary appliance only.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. The check of the Help page asks for a row with the action Cancel request, which exists only while a request is pending; it requests `NO:SUCH:PV:HELP`, a name that no IOC serves and that stays in Initial sampling, and adds no other name.
