#### M73 - Reaction of the archiver to a record that changes while it is archived

Origin: daff1b7 / M73
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #44 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/44)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The browser checks of the Browse PVs page and the integration tests run against PVs that do not change. A record of a control system changes while it is archived: its scan rate is set to another value, its unit, precision or limits are edited, or the IOC is started with the same name on a record of another type. The engine has code for the last case (`EPICS_V3_PV` drops a sample whose DBR type differs from the type of the PV, `PVMetrics` counts it, and `getPVsByDroppedEventsTypeChange` and the `N lost` of the State column report it), and no recorded check runs the three changes against the real appliance. Read on 2026-10-16: the sample script `listTypeChanges.bash` selects its PVs with the same report. The PVA path (`EPICS_V4_PV`) fixes the type from the first structure of the channel and has no such drop: an event of another structure is converted with the old constructor. No existing test drives a real type change; the script tests use a fake server and `EPICS_V4_PVDisconnectSeamTest` leaves the callback empty.

##### Scope

- Test PVs: the fixed list of M72 (decision of 2026-10-17), on a temporary appliance that starts fresh for every run; the kept appliance and its IOC are not changed by this item. A name serves one check only, so that a check never depends on what another left:
  - T1: `SR:BPM:02:X` archived by monitor and `SR:BPM:02:Y` archived by scan (their values change at every scan).
  - T2: `SR:RF:CAV2:TEMP` with the defaults of the archiver and `SR:RF:CAV2:POWER` with the property subscription (`useDBEProperties`) turned on.
  - T3 and T4: `SR:BPM:04:X` changed to an integer record, `SR:BPM:04:Y` to a string record and `SR:BPM:03:X` to a waveform record, all archived over Channel Access.
  - T5: `SR:BPM:03:Y` archived over PVAccess (`pva://`) and changed to an integer record.
- The second IOC database is built from `ConsoleChartPVs.db` with these four records replaced by records of the same names and other types; it is a test resource and no record outside the list is added.
- The scan rate: `.SCAN` of the periodic record is changed with `caput` to a faster and a slower period while the PV is archived; the spacing of the stored samples is read back.
- The unit, the precision and the limits: `.EGU`, `.PREC` and the limit fields are changed with `caput` in three conditions (the channel stays connected with the defaults; it stays connected with the property subscription on; the IOC restarts); the type information, the Details window and the meta fields of `getData` are read back.
- The record type over Channel Access: the IOC is restarted with the record name on a record of another DBR type; the dropped samples, the counter, the State column and the data before and after are read back.
- The way out: the PV is paused, its type is changed in the Maintenance window (`changeTypeForPV`) and the PV is resumed; the counter, the new samples and a read of one window across the change are checked.
- The record type over PVAccess: the same change on a PV archived with `pva://`; the counters, the log, the stored data and the State column are read back.
- The expected reaction of each change is written in the Test Plan from the code of the engine; what the code does not settle is marked as to be observed, and a deviation from the expected reaction is a finding and gets an issue. No code is changed in this item.

Out of scope: the repair of any deviation found; a change of the PV name (rename); the loss of the connection and the IOC restart without a change, which the existing connection checks cover; the Browse PVs page itself.

##### Completion Criteria

- For each of the changes (scan rate, unit with precision and limits in three conditions, record type over Channel Access with its way out, record type over PVAccess) the check and its observed result are recorded in this detail, with the data window, the counters and the reading of the type information before and after.
- Every deviation from the expected reaction is filed as an issue with the steps that reproduce it, and every observation marked as to be observed has its result written down.
- The checks run through the real shipped path, on packaged WARs with a soft IOC on a temporary appliance, and a rerun starts from a fresh appliance and needs no state that an earlier run left.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- No M or G dependency.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. The owner asked for this check as an item of its own, apart from the chart widget, and remarked that the checks should use PVs that are already archived and keep their earlier data.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. The owner decided that the record type check includes the way out (pause, change of type, resume and a read across the change) and a PVAccess case, after the review of the plan found that the Channel Access path drops every event of the new type until the type is changed in the archiver, and that the PVAccess path has no such drop.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. The names of the checks are fixed in Scope: the first draft named two PVs for eight cases.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. T1 uses `SR:BPM:02:X` and `SR:BPM:02:Y` and not `FAST:SIG:1` and `FAST:SIG:2`: the first run showed that the two FAST records compute from `SR:TICK` only, so their value changes once a second whatever the scan period (the description of the records says 10 Hz). This changes two names of the accepted plan; the owner confirmed the change on 2026-10-17 and the Test Plan names the two BPM records.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-17. The second IOC database is built in two steps, `meta.db` (the changed control data of the two `SR:RF:CAV2` records, for the restart of T2) and `types.db` (`meta.db` with four records replaced, for T3 to T5); each run starts a new run folder, because the launcher keeps the configuration and the stores of a folder.
- Record 2026-10-17: the kept appliance stopped at 15:15:28 PDT because the setup script of these checks ended every local appliance launcher and not only the temporary one; it archived nothing until it was started again at 16:28 PDT (a gap of 73 minutes in the archived history; the earlier data and the IOC were not affected). The restart needed other WARs, because `./mvnw clean verify` had emptied `target/`, which the kept WAR folder pointed to; it now runs the build aa-20261017-aa6ca27f from a folder of copies. The scripts stop only the launcher of their own port base and their own IOC.
- The plan is accepted and implemented; the findings below are to be filed as issues.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-17; owner accepted the plan with the way out and the PVAccess case
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-17; owner directed the implementation of this plan; commits, pushes and issue changes need their own authority
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. The expected reaction of each change is written in the Test Plan from the code of the engine (done 2026-10-17); the observations marked as to be observed are settled by the runs. No code.
2. The fixture of a run: a script that starts a fresh temporary appliance from the packaged WARs, starts the soft IOC and archives the fixed list; the second IOC database built from `ConsoleChartPVs.db`; the checks as scripts that drive `caput`, the IOC restart, the management calls and the pages. Check: a dry run archives the list and a second run starts from nothing.
3. Run T1 to T5 on packaged WARs and record the results; file an issue for each deviation. Check: T1 to T5.

#### M74 - Plot limit note and bulk Plot controls in the PV table

Origin: daff1b7 / M74
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

Read on 2026-10-17 in `js/browse.js` and `css/browse.css`: when 5 PVs are plotted, the other Plot boxes of the table are disabled, the pointer over one shows the not-allowed cursor, and the only explanation is the text of its tooltip ("At most 5 PVs are plotted at a time. Turn another Plot box off first.", `browse.js:725`). No note is on the page while the limit is reached, and a disabled box takes no click, so the page cannot answer an attempt to turn a sixth box on. The table has no control that turns Plot boxes on or off together: each is turned off one by one. The counts are in two places: "Plotted n of at most 5" in the left panel and "table x/100" in the heading of the table.

##### Scope

- The message of the Plot boxes that are over the limit is made stronger and stays where it is: the boxes remain `disabled` with the not-allowed cursor. The words say that at most 5 PVs are drawn and that a Plot box has to be turned off first. A disabled box takes neither the pointer nor a tap, so the box over the limit is made transparent to them (`pointer-events: none`) and the cell under it takes them. The tooltip is on the whole cell, the cell has the not-allowed cursor, and the same words are shown as a visible note beside the counters of the heading of the table, as a status for assistive technology: while the pointer is over the cell, and, on a touch screen, from a tap on the cell until the next tap elsewhere or until a Plot box is turned off. The note floats in the top margin above the heading and takes no room, because a note that took room moved the table down under the pointer, the pointer then stood on the cell of the row above, the note went and the table moved back (seen on 2026-10-17 with a note in the line of the heading). The boxes under the limit show nothing.
- Two controls beside "table x/100", for the Plot boxes only: First 5 turns the Plot boxes of the first five rows of the table, in the order of the table, on and every other Plot box off (with fewer than five rows, every row); Deselect all turns every Plot box off. Each is disabled while it has nothing to do (First 5 with an empty table, Deselect all with no Plot box on).
- Two more controls in the same place, added on 2026-10-17 at the owner's request: Plotted only, a toggle that shows only the rows whose Plot box is on and hides the others until it is pressed again (the counter reads the shown rows of the total); and Clear selection, which unticks every chosen PV so that the table is empty and the chart shows the message for no plotted PV. Each is disabled while it has nothing to do, and each has a title that says what it does.
- The address of the page keeps the plotted PVs as it does for one Plot box, so a link reproduces the choice; the Plotted only toggle is not kept in the address.
- Two controls under the count of the Find panel, added on 2026-10-17 at the owner's request, which was about this panel: Selected only, a toggle that shows in the list only the selected PVs instead of the matches until it is pressed again (the count line then reads the selected PVs shown); and Clear selection, which clears every selection as the control of the table does. Each is disabled while nothing is selected, each has a title, and the toggle is not kept in the address. The two controls of the table stay.
- The manual and the Help page name the six controls and the note.

Out of scope: a change of the limit of 5 or 100; the chart; the prefix buttons of the Find panel (their explanation is M65); the other pages.

##### Completion Criteria

#### M76 - Archiving continues across a change of the record

Origin: daff1b7 / M76
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #48 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/48)
Status: Deferred

##### Summary

M73 observed, on 2026-10-17 and again on 2026-10-18 on the one IOC and the one appliance of D44, that the engine detects a change of the archived record but stops at counting: a record that posts faster than the rate estimated at the archive request loses most events to a sample buffer of 11 (T1); a changed unit, precision or limit reaches the archiver only through the property subscription or, for the unit and the precision, at a reconnect, and the display limits are never read again (T2); a record that comes back under the same name with another type has every event dropped and counted while the type information keeps the old type (T3, T5); the way out is manual, pause and `changeTypeForPV` and resume, converts the history (a double 0.0057 becomes the integer 0) and refuses a string or a waveform with HTTP 500 (T4). The role of the archiver is the opposite: to keep the signal without a gap (D45).

##### Scope

- The engine detects each change that M73 names and goes on storing under the new condition from the instant of the change, on its own: a changed type opens a new type from that instant, a faster record gets a buffer and a sampling that follow it, changed metadata is read again.
- The earlier samples stay readable as they were stored: a PV has a type boundary on its time axis, and the stores and the retrieval know it, because a PB file holds one type.
- The console and the manual show the boundary and the change.

Out of scope until the plan is written: the exact store layout of the boundary; the policy for a change the engine cannot follow.

##### Completion Criteria

- The five checks of M73, run again, store the signal through each change without a manual step, and a window of `getData` across the change returns the earlier samples with their stored type and the later samples with the new one.
- No event is dropped for a reason the engine could have followed; what is dropped is logged with its reason.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- M73 is the observation this row answers; D45 defers the row to the next major release (Decision Date: 2026-10-17) and limits this release to M77.
- Transition: Deferred on 2026-10-17 by D45; it returns to Not started when the next major release opens.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: draft
Plan Acceptance: none
Implementation Authorization: none
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. Design of the type boundary in the stores and the retrieval, with the data-change rules of the PB files.
2. The engine reactions, one per change of M73.
3. The console and the manual.

##### GitHub Projection

Title: Archiving continues across a change of the record

Body: The engine detects a change of an archived record but stops at counting, so a change on the IOC side ends the recording of the signal until an operator acts. Observed on a local appliance with a soft IOC: a record that posts faster than the rate estimated at the archive request loses most events to a sample buffer of 11 (58 samples and 445 lost in 46 s at 10 Hz); a changed unit, precision or limit reaches the archiver only through the property subscription or at a reconnect, and the display limits are never read again; a record that comes back under the same name with another type has every event dropped and counted while the type information keeps the old type; the way out, pause, `changeTypeForPV`, resume, converts the history (a double 0.0057 becomes the integer 0) and answers HTTP 500 for a string or a waveform (`UnsupportedOperationException` in `ThruNumberAndStringConversion`). The archiver should keep the signal without a gap: detect the change and go on storing under the new condition from the instant of the change, with the earlier samples readable as they were stored, which needs a type boundary on the time axis of a PV that the stores and the retrieval know. Planned for the next major release; in the current release the engine logs the change and pauses a PV whose type changed.

#### M77 - Log and pause on a record that changes

Origin: daff1b7 / M77
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

Read on 2026-10-18 in the engine logs of the M73 runs: none of the five changes writes a line to the engine console log (`grep -c` of each PV name counted 18 lines, all from the archive request and the connection). The only signs are the counters of `getPVDetails`, the dropped-events reports and the `N lost` mark of the Browse PVs page. A PV whose type changed stays `Being archived` and drops every event; nothing stops it.

##### Scope

- A log line for each change the engine detects, naming the PV and the change, one line per PV per change and not per event: WARN at the first event dropped for a changed type (with the old and the new type), where both the Channel Access monitor and the sample buffer drop it; WARN at the first event dropped for a full sample buffer in each write period (with the capacity, the sampling period of the request and the measured event rate), cleared when the buffer is written so that the next period writes one line again; the INFO line that `MetaInfo.updateTypeInfo` already writes for a changed unit or precision stays as it is (the limits are #47).
- A PV whose type changed is paused by the engine after the first dropped event, because nothing of it can be stored any more: the pause of the engine also marks the type information paused and saves the reason in its `pauseReason` field (empty for an operator's pause), it runs outside the monitor callback thread, `getPVStatus` reads Paused, and the Details window shows the reason. A PV that loses events to a full buffer is not paused, because part of the signal still arrives.
- The manual's section on a record that changes names the log lines, the pause and the reason.

Out of scope: following the change (M76); a change of the buffer, the sampling or the type information beyond the new field; the console beyond the Details window row.

##### Completion Criteria

- The checks of M73, run again, leave one WARN line per PV for the type change and one WARN line per PV per write period for the buffer loss in the engine log, with the PV name and the change in it, and nothing per event.
- After the type change of T3 the three Channel Access PVs and the PVAccess PV are Paused within one write period, `getPVTypeInfo` carries the reason in `pauseReason`, the Details window shows it, and the dropped count stops growing; the PV of T1 stays Being archived.
- The suite passes, with a test of the engine that pauses a PV on a changed type and keeps the reason, and the manual names the lines and the pause.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- Depends on M73 (the observations and the checks). D45 (Decision Date: 2026-10-17) limits the reaction in this release to the log line and the pause. Issue #46 asks for the log line of the buffer loss and the manual text; this row delivers them, and #48 holds the full reaction of M76.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. The reason of a pause made by the engine is kept in a new field `pauseReason` of `PVTypeInfo` (empty for a pause made by an operator), saved with the type information and shown by the Details window; the type information is JSON, so the field is compatible with the stored data (option 1 of the review of 2026-10-18).
- Decision Date: 2026-10-18. A PV whose events are lost to the full buffer (T1) is only logged, not paused, because the signal still arrives in part and a shorter sampling period cures it; only a PV whose type changed is paused.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted

#### M78 - Refuse optimized as a reducedata operator

Origin: daff1b7 / M78
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #49 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/49)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

A store URL with `reducedata=optimized_N` is accepted, but the ETL reduces into 15-minute bins whatever N says, or keeps the raw samples when the partition holds N samples or fewer: `Optimized.initialize` reads N only, the bin width is set in `estimateMemoryConsumption` from the range of a retrieval request, which the ETL does not call, so the inner `Statistics` keeps `DEFAULT_SUMMARIZING_INTERVAL` (900 s). `optimized` and `optimLastSample` are defined by a retrieval range and have no meaning on a store; the time-bin operators (`firstSample_N`, `mean_N` and the others with a bin width in seconds) are the ones that apply.

##### Scope

- `PlainPBStoragePlugin.initialize` refuses `optimized` and `optimLastSample`, with or without `_N`, as the value of `reducedata`: it throws the `IOException` that `StoragePluginURLParser` passes on, whose message names the parameter, the value and the form of the operators that apply (an operator with a bin width in seconds, such as `firstSample_3600` or `mean_60`), so that the store is not created.
- The `reducedata` row of the Stores table of `docs/book/src/configuration.md` names the form of the operators that apply and says that `optimized` does not.

Out of scope: a range-free form of `optimized` for the ETL; the `pp` parameter.

##### Completion Criteria

- A store URL with `reducedata=optimized`, `reducedata=optimized_500` or `reducedata=optimLastSample_100` fails to initialize with an `IOException` whose message names the value and the form of the operators that apply; a unit test covers the three forms.
- A store URL with `reducedata=firstSample_3600` initializes as before and the existing reducedata tests pass.
- The PVs of a policy that carries a refused URL cannot use that store: the ETL logs one ERROR line per PV at its registration and the retrieval and the engine report the `IOException` where they parse the URL, instead of reducing silently into 900-second bins; the book row says that `optimized` does not apply.
- The book row names the form of the operators that apply.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): moved from the Backlog to the Milestone table to land before the merge of `modernize`.
- Decision Date 2026-10-19: M78 and M79 change the same lines of `initialize` and share one unit test class, so they are built together and land in one commit that closes #49 and #50; each row keeps its own completion criteria and closes on its own.
- Found on 2026-10-19 while answering the environment session's question on `optimized_N` in `reducedata`.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-19: the owner accepted the plan with the two refinements of its review (the message names the operators that apply by their form, and the completion criteria state what a refused URL does to the PVs of its policy) and the joint build with M79 ("그렇게 합시다. 네가 제안하는 대로 하자. 반영 다 하고.")

A store URL that carries both `reducedata` and `pp` is accepted; `appendData` applies the `reducedata` operator first and writes the reduced events as the `.pb` file, and the `pp` caches are then computed from that file, so a cache named for a raw-data operator holds the operator applied to reduced data and the retrieval serves it as such. #### M80 - Delete the post-processor files of a moved partition

Origin: daff1b7 / M80
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #51 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/51)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

When the ETL moves a partition out of a store that carries `pp`, `markForDeletion` deletes the `.pb` file of the partition and nothing deletes its post-processor files, so one file per partition and operator accumulates for every PV of such a store. Observed by the environment session with the shipped plugin at 65245250 (an MTS with `pp=mean_60` keeps `2026_01_01_10.mean_60` after its `2026_01_01_10.pb` moved to the LTS) and read in the code: `getETLStreams` and `getETLStreamsForDeletion` list `.pb` paths only.

##### Scope

- `markForDeletion` deletes, when it has deleted the `.pb` file of a partition, the post-processor file of that partition for every operator of `postProcessorUserArgs`: the file whose name is the `.pb` name with its trailing extension replaced by the operator's (`PostProcessors.findPostProcessor(arg).getExtension()`, as `commitETLAppendData` names the files it writes; the suffix alone is replaced, not every `.pb` of the path, which the existing lookup of missing caches does; an operator the registry does not know is skipped with the existing ERROR line); a missing file is not an error; when the `.pb` file is kept (its size changed), the post-processor files are kept with it. The path is resolved through `context.getPaths()`, so the uncompressed and the `ZIP_PER_PV` modes take the same route; for a zip store this reaches the explicit deletion only, because a zip store that is the source of a move keeps the moved partition itself (its `ETLInfo` key lacks the `jar:` form), a defect of the zip source that D47 leaves to the Backlog.
- `getETLStreamsForDeletion` lists the post-processor files of the partitions it returns as `ETLInfo` rows with their sizes, so `deleteETLStream` removes them under its contract (a path and an observed size) and the explicit deletion of a PV's data removes them too.

Out of scope: the files left behind by earlier moves; the post-processor files of the destination store.

##### Completion Criteria

- An ETL test over two hops (STS to a MTS that carries `pp=mean_60`, then that MTS to the LTS), run with the shipped `ETLJob` on PlainPB stores, moves a partition out of the MTS and leaves neither its `.pb` file nor its `.mean_60` file there, while both files of the partition still in the MTS are untouched.
- The explicit deletion of a PV's data from a store with `pp` leaves no file of that PV, the post-processor files among them, for an uncompressed store and for a `ZIP_PER_PV` store (its entries).
- A `merge` store in front of a PlainPB store deletes the same files, since `MergeDedupStoragePlugin` delegates `markForDeletion`, `getETLStreamsForDeletion` and `deleteETLStream` to the store behind it; the three delegating methods are unchanged in the diff and the existing merge store tests pass.
- The `pp` row of the Stores table in `docs/book/src/configuration.md` says that the post-processor files of a moved partition leave the store with it.
- `ETLPostProcessorTest` (the caches computed on the destination) and the ETL and PlainPB test suites pass.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- D46 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): moved from the Backlog to the Milestone table to land before the merge of `modernize`.
- Found on 2026-10-19 from the environment session's observation of the leftover file.
- D47 (Decision Date 2026-10-19): the check of the two hops found that a `ZIP_PER_PV` store that is the source of a move keeps the partition it moved (the `ETLInfo` key of `getETLStreams` lacks the `jar:` form); the owner left that defect to the Backlog (M83) because the site uses no zip store and a zip store sits last in a chain, and the book says so; this row covers the zip store for the explicit deletion only.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Status: accepted
Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-19: the owner accepted the plan after three third-person reviews and three second-person passes of the same day, all findings applied (the suffix-only name of the post-processor file, the merge store's delegation, the ZIP entries, the two as-if times with the check after the first hop, the verifiable criteria) ("수락과 구현승인")
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-19: the owner authorized the implementation of the accepted plan in the same words; commits, pushes and issue changes need their own authority
Superseded Plan Artifacts: none

1. A private helper of `PlainPBStoragePlugin` that returns the post-processor paths of a `.pb` path (one per operator of `postProcessorUserArgs`, by `getExtension`, through `context.getPaths()`); `markForDeletion` deletes them after the `.pb` file, and `getETLStreamsForDeletion` lists them with their sizes. Check: T1.
2. A test class `PlainPBPostProcessorCleanupTest` over the shipped `ETLJob` and PlainPB stores: STS HOUR to MTS HOUR with `pp=mean_60` to LTS YEAR, two hour partitions of data written with the shipped writer, one `ETLJob` run per hop: the first hop with an as-if time past both partitions, so both reach the MTS and get their `.pb` and `.mean_60` files there, the second hop with an as-if time between the end of the older partition and the end of the newer, so only the older moves on; the MTS folder listed after the first run, after the second run and after the explicit deletion of the PV from the MTS; and, for a MTS in `ZIP_PER_PV` mode, the first hop and the explicit deletion with the entries of the archive listed. Check: T1.
3. The book: a sentence on the `pp` row that the files of a moved partition leave with it, and a `compress` row that names `ZIP_PER_PV` for the last store only, since a zip source keeps the partition it moved. Check: T1.

##### Test Plan

##### Summary

Seven places of the shipped console, the retrieval API, the ETL and the sample scripts give a wrong result or none, and three leftovers remain beside them; found on 2026-10-19 when the pages of the book were compared with the code and the console figures were retaken. The Operations page reads `"Yes"` of `getLostConnectionsReport` as not `"true"` and shows every PV as not connected (observed); `getDataForPVs` carries the operator of one PV to the PVs after it (observed); `getPausedPVsReport` repeats `?limit=` and the per-appliance call ignores it; `getPVStatus.py` rejects the state `Held`; an unknown or malformed retrieval operator is answered as a success or as an empty 200 or a bare 404 (observed); `getMetadata` answers an empty 200 when the engine has no metadata; and a consolidation requested while the ETL stops waits for ever when the stop drops its task (forced with the shipped classes: a delete queued behind a busy worker of another driver on the same index stayed blocked after 60 seconds). The leftovers are the `input#delete` rules of `main.css`, the directory-stack output of three PB scripts and the word "cluster" in page text.

##### Scope

- `operations.js` compares `currentlyConnected` with `"yes"` ignoring case, the idiom of `judge.js`.
- `getDataForPVs` and the multi-PV path of `PvaGetPVData` (the two loops that keep `postProcessorUserArg`) take the operator of each PV from its own function-call name (`mean_60(A)` and `mean(A,60)`) or from the `pp` of the request, one value per iteration, never the value of an earlier PV; the lists `postProcessors` and `postProcessorUserArgs` agree.
- `PausedPVsReport` builds the per-appliance URL with one `limit`; `GetPausedPVsForThisAppliance` declares `@BPLParam` `limit` and applies it; a `limit` that is not an integer of at least 1 answers HTTP 400; an absent `limit` returns all, as the other caller (`DefaultConfigService`) needs; `scripting.md` lists the parameter.
- `archiverClient.py` knows `Held`.
- A check of the retrieval operator string, a new method of `PostProcessors` (the store `pp` URLs keep `findPostProcessor` as it is). A blank `pp` and `pb` mean raw data. `twoweek` and `extraFields` are accepted as server-internal names, because `PBOverHTTPStoragePlugin` sends the extension of the request post-processor to the other appliance (the private name of `ExtraFieldsPostProcessor` becomes a constant). Otherwise the name before the first underscore must be a registered key (`meanx` is not one), and the argument must parse and lie in the domain of the operator: an integer of at least 1 for `firstSample`, `lastSample`, `firstFill`, `lastFill`, every statistics operator, `caplotbinning`, the bin of `flyers` and `ignoreflyers`, `nth`, and the N of `optimized` and `optimLastSample`; a finite number above 0 for the second argument of `flyers` and `ignoreflyers`; a finite number of at least 0 for `deadBand`; `ncount` takes no argument. `mean_`, `mean__5`, `mean_60.5`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are bad arguments. `getData` and `getDataForPVs` answer HTTP 400 with a message that names the operator and the reason, before any data is read; the message is in the body. `PvaGetPVData` (single path before the type info lookup, multi path) throws `PvaActionException` with the same message. D48.
- `GetPVMetaData` answers 200 with the type information alone when the engine answer is null, and reads the engine with `getURLContentAsJSONObject(url, false)` so that a paused PV logs no error. D48.
- `PBThreeTierETLPVLookup.consolidate`: the task is claimed exactly once. The worker-side body claims it only while `workersStopped` is false and the worker thread is not interrupted. The waiter waits in a timed loop; once `workersStopped` is true and the task is unclaimed, the calling thread claims it and runs it, but only when the pass driver runs no job for that PV (`getCurrentJobPv()`); when it does, the caller waits for that job at most the stop wait, then logs an ERROR and returns without running. The hook's `takeQueued` loop gets the same guard. An interrupted wait restores the flag, stops waiting for this and the later indexes without running inline, and logs an ERROR naming the PV and the index. A task that a worker claimed before the stop is waited for at most the stop wait after the stop; before the stop the wait has no limit, as today. A rejected `execute` lets the calling thread claim the task. D48.
- `docs/design-etl-pass-scheduler.md`: the sentences about the inline run after the stop and "no PV is processed by two jobs at once" (Components), the clause about consolidations "still queued on a worker whose job is still running" (the stop), D12 and R4 say what the code does; no new decision row.
- The leftovers. The rules for `input#delete` and the comment above them leave `main.css`. `validate.sh`, `repair.sh` and `printTimes.sh` send `pushd` and `popd` to `/dev/null`. The page text says "installation" where it means this installation or another one: the lead of `operations.html`, the cards of `operations.js` ("this cluster", "every appliance of the cluster") and of `external.js` (the other installation in the first cards, this installation in the restart messages), `help.html`; line 803 of `operations.js` keeps the data key `cluster` and changes the label only; comments, variable names and `getAppliancesInCluster` stay.
- The book: `retrieval.md` states the answers for an unknown or malformed operator, the names accepted as raw and as internal, and that `optimLastSample` over a range shorter than its N seconds still answers an empty body (unchanged); `scripting.md` lists `limit`.
- The Operations figure is retaken while all PVs are connected, before the IOC stop of T1.

Out of scope: the zip source of an ETL move (M83); the name `disconnectCheckTimeoutInMinutes` and any other key; the 28 API texts of the generated reference that say "cluster"; the empty answer of `optimLastSample` over a short range; any change of an API beyond the cases above.

##### Completion Criteria

- On an appliance whose PVs are connected, "Connected now" of "PVs that drop out most" reads "yes" for each listed PV and reads "no" for a PV whose IOC is stopped, checked on the page; the Operations figure of the book shows the corrected column.
- `getDataForPVs` and the multi-PV path of `PvaGetPVData` return `B` as `B` alone returns it for `pv=mean_60(A)&pv=B`, for `pv=mean(A,60)&pv=B` and with a request `pp`.
- `getPausedPVsReport?limit=n` and `getPausedPVsForThisAppliance?limit=n` over more than n paused PVs return n; a bad `limit` answers 400; no `limit` returns all; `scripting.md` lists `limit`.
- `getPVStatus.py` reports `Held` as a status with exit status 0.
- `bogus`, `meanx`, `mean_abc`, `mean_0`, `mean_60.5` and `nth_-1` answer HTTP 400 with a message in the body on `getData` and `getDataForPVs`; an empty or blank `pp`, `pp=pb`, `pp=twoweek`, `pp=extraFields` and `mean_60` answer 200; a request with `usereduced=true` for a PV on the other appliance of the two-appliance fixture still returns its data; `PvaGetPVData` fails the call on archived PVs with the message of the check (the PVAccess client library writes the message of a failed RPC to its log and does not return it to the caller); `MultiPVClusterRetrievalTest` passes; `retrieval.md` states the answers.
- `getMetadata` of a paused PV answers 200 with its type information, which says it is paused; the answer for a connected PV is unchanged; no error with a stack trace is logged for the paused PV.
- With `ETLPassStopWaitSeconds` 0, after `shutdown()` and after `manualControlForUnitTests()`, a delete queued behind a busy worker of another driver on the same index returns within a time limit with the data of the PV moved by the calling thread, no PV is processed by two jobs at once, an interrupted wait is logged and leaves the flag set, and `design-etl-pass-scheduler.md` says what the code does.
- The page text has no "cluster" outside the stated lines, the three PB scripts print no directory stack, the rules of `input#delete` are gone.
- `scripts/ui-static-checks.bash`, the default suite, the slow test of T7 and the integration set pass, and the book builds with no broken link.
- Each test that exercises a fixed defect fails on the unfixed code first, and the failure is recorded.

Notes of the run. The integration run reached the kept appliance: the PVAccess classes find the RPC services by name search, the kept appliance answered, and 25 PVs named `PV:...:PvaGetPVDataTest:...` were archived there. They were paused and deleted with their data at 2026-10-20 01:01 PDT and `getAllPVs` read 131 again. `PvaGetPVDataTest` was then run with the kept appliance stopped, as `TESTING.md` prescribes, in two windows (01:15 to 01:26 PDT and 01:28 to 01:37 PDT); `TESTING.md` now says so. The kept appliance was stopped and started four times in all, at 00:58 and 01:04 PDT for the new WARs and the cleared counters, and in the two windows, always by its own launcher with a clean stop and a ready status after 36 seconds. Deleting a paused PV leaves the engine's paused PV count raised until the next restart: `ArchiveEngine` increments it at the pause and decrements it only at the resume.

#### M85 - Protect the retrieval application against memory exhaustion

Origin: daff1b7 / M85
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: #54 (https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epicsarchiverap-maven/issues/54)
Status: In progress

##### Summary

The retrieval web application exhausted its heap on 2026-10-20 while `retrieval.md` was checked against the kept appliance, on a retrieval JVM with a 256 MB heap. The `console.log` of that run (started 01:36, poller ended 10:47, restarted 11:03) holds 47 `getData` requests that ended in `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` and 21 that ended in `OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit`, and further heap-space errors on PVAccess, Hazelcast and Tomcat threads, from 43 operator-argument combinations (`mean_2147483647`, `optimized_2147483647`, `optimLastSample_2147484`, `optimized_100000000`, `optimLastSample_3000000` and `optimLastSample_2000000` among them) on four PVs archived as monitor with a period of 1 s and created two to six days before; the log holds no request parameters, and the range of about 80 days is known for the `optimLastSample_2000000` request from the report of #54 when it was filed. The first heap-space error came from `optimized_100000000`, was caught per request (`ExecutionException` in `evaluateEventStreamFutures`) and the JVM kept answering; Tomcat logged a heap-space error at 10:01:35, the PVAccess UDP receiver and TCP listener threads died of it and Hazelcast tasks failed, and the poller thread of the Tomcat connector died by 10:47:05 after `optimLastSample_100000` and `optimLastSample_1000000`, after which the ping URL, the viewer page and `getData` got no answer while the process stayed up; the management application kept answering and only a restart restored the service. Whether one request alone stops the service is a hypothesis for T1 and T3; that any client that can reach the retrieval port can stop it with a few requests, by mistake or on purpose, is observed. The main code has no protection: `DataRetrievalServlet` and `PvaGetPVData` call `estimateMemoryConsumption` and only write the value to the debug log, the only reader of the heap is `ProcessMetrics`, which records the used percentage once a minute for a report, and the code has no `MemoryPoolMXBean`, no limit on running requests and no handling of a failed allocation, and an exception inside the answer is logged and swallowed, without a status in HTTP and as a success in PVAccess (read in the code on 2026-10-20). The heap-space errors left no allocation frame (the JVM wrote the error without a stack trace), so where the heap ran out is not recorded; frames exist for 4 of the VM-limit errors only, in the preallocation `ArrayListEventStream(numberOfPoints, desc)` (`Optimized.java:168`, `OptimizedWithLastSample.java:224`) for an argument near 2^31. That array is one reference per point, about 8 MB at 2 million points. The code reading gives the first hypothesis for the rest: `consolidatedData` of `SummaryStatsPostProcessor`, a `LinkedHashMap<Long, SummaryValue>` with one entry per bin, which `optimized` and `optimLastSample` build over the bins of the range; for `optimLastSample_2000000` over 80 days the bin is 3 s wide, which gives about 2.3 million bins. How much each structure holds per bin or per point has not been measured. The JDK and Tomcat 9 provide the pieces of the protection (read on 2026-10-20): the JVM options `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` and `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError`, the valves `SemaphoreValve` (a 503 above a concurrency) and `StuckThreadDetectionValve` (an interrupt after a threshold), `MemoryPoolMXBean.getCollectionUsage()` (the memory left after the most recent collection), and `com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean.getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes()` (the bytes the request thread allocated), so no library is needed.

##### Scope

Four layers, all from the JDK and Tomcat 9 (D50), on by default (D49).

- JVM options, for the four JVMs: `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` and `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError` with `-XX:HeapDumpPath` in the logs folder, in the launcher (`JVM_COMMON_OPTIONS` of `scripts/run-local-appliance.bash`) and in the `JAVA_OPTS` of the installation page. A JVM that throws an `OutOfMemoryError` ends with exit status 3 and leaves a dump, instead of staying up without answering, and it does so whether or not a request handler would catch the error and whether or not the heap is full: a `Requested array size exceeds VM limit` error ends it too (observed on 2026-10-21 on JDK 21 with a program that caught the error; the catch block never ran). The console then holds a line `Terminating due to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError`. The local launcher watches its children (`ensure_children` in its main loop) and ends the whole appliance when one exits, so under the launcher an `OutOfMemoryError` in any of the four stops all four; under the installation page, where each instance is its own process, only that instance ends. Both are stated in the pages. A dump can be larger than the heap (734 MB for a 512 MB heap that a request filled, observed by T3 on 2026-10-21; 36 MB for a 64 MB heap full of live data and 5 MB for the VM-limit error in a small program), and each exit writes a new file named with the process id, so repeated exits fill the logs folder; the pages say so next to the option.
- Tomcat valves, for retrieval and management: `org.apache.catalina.valves.SemaphoreValve` with `block="false"` and `highConcurrencyStatus="503"` limits the concurrent requests, and `org.apache.catalina.valves.StuckThreadDetectionValve` with `interruptThreadThreshold` interrupts a request that runs too long. They are declared in a `META-INF/context.xml` of each of the two WARs, the retrieval WAR and the management WAR (owner decision (3)), with attributes of the form `${name:-default}` so that a system property gives a test a low value; the concurrency and the thresholds come from the measurement. A valve declared on the context applies to every URL of the web application, including the BPL calls that the other web applications make to management and to retrieval and the static files, so the concurrency counts those callers; the stuck-thread valve interrupts a thread at the first background tick after the threshold, so the interrupt is delivered between the threshold and the threshold plus the `backgroundProcessorDelay` of its container (observed on 2026-10-21 on Tomcat 9.0.121: threshold 1 s with a delay of 4 s interrupted at 3.7 s, threshold 1 s with a delay of 1 s at 1.7 s), an `interruptThreadThreshold` below the threshold acts as the threshold, and the engine default of the delay is 10 s. This layer covers HTTP only; the PVAccess RPC server (`PVAServer` of `PvaDataRetrievalServlet`) is not behind the Tomcat pipeline, and how it bounds concurrent calls is recorded by T2. T5 verifies the valve's interrupt delivery; T6 and T7 verify that the retrieval code then stops at its next check and delivers the failure.
- Memory after garbage collection, in retrieval: a class in the retrieval package selects the old-generation heap pool (under G1 `G1 Old Gen`; in general the `MemoryPoolMXBean` of type heap with the largest maximum that supports a collection usage threshold; the young pools support it too, but their usage after a collection does not measure the live data of the requests) and, when a request is admitted, reads `getCollectionUsage().getUsed()`, the usage left after the most recent collection, which triggers no collection. `DataRetrievalServlet` (single and multi path), `GetDataAtTime` on its per-appliance path (`getDataAtTimeForAppliance`, which reads the stores; `getDataAtTime` only fans out over HTTP) and `PvaGetPVData` ask it before any data is read; when either that collection usage or the current old-generation usage from `getUsage().getUsed()` is above the admission threshold, the check asks for a collection (`System.gc()`) at most once per shared interval and reads the collection usage again, and only if it is still above the admission threshold is the request refused with HTTP 503 and a message that names the condition, or the PVAccess call refused (the error delivery item states what its caller sees). The collection request is needed because this value changes only when the pool is collected: on G1 it stayed at 171 MB, all of it garbage, for 80 s after the load ended with no or low allocation, and a JVM that refuses every request allocates nothing that would trigger the collection (observed on 2026-10-21 on JDK 21 with `-Xmx256m`; the launcher and the installation page set no `DisableExplicitGC`). A deployment that sets `-XX:+DisableExplicitGC` turns the collection request into nothing and the refusal outlasts the load again (observed on 2026-10-21: the usage after collection stayed at 177 MB after `System.gc()`; with `-XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent` it fell to 4 MB), so the class reads that option at start through `HotSpotDiagnosticMXBean.getVMOption("DisableExplicitGC")` and logs a WARN that names the consequence, and the pages say not to set it. The value also stays at 0 until the first old-generation collection, which G1 starts at 45% heap occupancy at first (`G1UseAdaptiveIHOP`, on by default, then moves that point with the allocation rate), so the admission threshold is chosen above the point that T1 records at the heap of the fixture. No listener is needed: the JDK notifies only the crossing upward, not the fall.
- Memory bound per request, in retrieval (D52): the size a request declares and the memory pressure decide, and the allocation of the request thread only chooses which request stops. The counter `com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean.getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes()` counts bytes allocated, not bytes held: a raw read of 2,592,000 events through the real `PlainPBStoragePlugin` allocated 105 MB, 42 bytes per event, and completed on a 64 MB heap (observed on 2026-10-21 on JDK 21), so a budget on the cumulative allocation would stop ordinary streaming requests, such as a year of 1 Hz data, and could not tell them from a request that accumulates. The structures that accumulate are sized by what the request declares, and that is checked at admission: the point count of `optimized` and `optimLastSample`, and the bins that an interval implies over the range, at the per-point and per-bin sizes T1 measures, are compared with the budget before the storage is read and before the preallocation `ArrayListEventStream(numberOfPoints, desc)`, because that preallocation is one allocation that no per-event check sees (an argument of 500,000,000 asks for a 2 GB array at once). While a request runs, a check every N events, at two places, reads the memory after collection of the layer above (with its rate-limited collection request) and compares it with a second threshold, higher than the admission threshold: an event stream that wraps the stream a storage plugin returns, before any post processor reads it, so one place covers every operator; and the output loops that build the answer, `consumeEventStreamAndOutputToMimeResponse` of `MergeDedupConsumer` for the HTTP path and of `PvaMergeDedupConsumer` for the PVAccess path (`doGetSinglePV` and `doGetMultiPV` of `PvaGetPVData`), with the same check in each, because a fill operator can produce more events than it reads. While the memory is above the second threshold, a request whose allocation since its start exceeds a floor stops with an error that names the condition, and a request below the floor continues; the counter is cumulative per thread and the Tomcat and PVAccess threads are reused, so the allocation of a request is the difference since its start. A streaming request therefore runs while there is no pressure; under pressure, every request above the floor stops at its next check and the others continue. A request thread that was interrupted by the valve stops at the same check. Retrieval runs the request on its own thread (`CurrentThreadExecutorService`), so the thread allocation is the allocation of the request. Where the JVM does not support thread allocation measurement, the existing `estimateMemoryConsumption` stands in for the allocation of the request.
- Error delivery, in HTTP and PVAccess retrieval: an error raised while the answer is being built, such as the pressure check in the streams or a failed preallocation, reaches the client. Today the catch blocks of `doGetSinglePV` and `doGetMultiPV` in `DataRetrievalServlet` (lines 498, 555, 993 and 1049) log the exception and set no status, the catch blocks of `doGetSinglePV` and `doGetMultiPV` in `PvaGetPVData` (lines 380, 392, 438, 913, 926 and 967) log it and return the partial structure as a success, and after a failed preallocation `getConsolidatedEventStream` dereferences the null `allEvents` (`Optimized.java:124`, `OptimizedWithLastSample.java:157`); the `console.log` of the retrieval instance shows that 37 times, 36 of them in the run of the summary, 23 in `Optimized` and 14 in `OptimizedWithLastSample`. The HTTP response is committed at the first `flushBuffer` or when the buffer fills, not when the content type is set, so a failed preallocation, which happens before any event is written, leaves the response uncommitted and the client receives 200 with an empty answer in each of the nine formats (observed by T3 on 2026-10-21: `[ ]` for `json`, `jplot` and `qw`, one byte for `csv`, nothing for `txt`, `mat` and `raw`, `<data> </data>` for `flx`, 12 bytes for `svg`), while a pressure check that fires later finds it committed (T7 confirms what the client receives). Step 6 splits the delivery by `resp.isCommitted()`: an error status with a message while the response is not committed, and once committed the connection is closed so that the body is cut short (owner decision (2)); the PVAccess call is failed with a `PvaActionException` that carries the message, because its structure is sent at the end. The caller does not receive that message: the client library (`core-pva` 5.0.5, `RPCRequest.handleResponse`) logs it and leaves the call without an answer, so the caller sees its own timeout (observed on 2026-10-21 with a real server and client: no answer after 8 s, the message in the client log; `PvaGetPVDataTest` asserts the failure the same way). The catch blocks named above and the null guard are part of this item.
- `OptimizedWithLastSample` computes its interval without the `int` overflow of `1000 * numberOfPoints`.
- Measurement before the values, in the test JVM: a test runs the real `PlainPBStoragePlugin` and the real post processors over generated data (`GenerateData`) for the query class (a large argument of `optimLastSample` and `optimized` over a long range; a statistics operator with a small interval over a long range), with the heap bounded by the surefire `-DargLine=-Xmx...`, reads `getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes()` on the same thread around each run and takes `jcmd GC.class_histogram` of the test JVM; the counter of a request that runs in another JVM cannot be read from outside. The budget, the admission threshold, the second threshold and the allocation floor are fractions of `Runtime.maxMemory()`, the concurrency is a count and the stuck thresholds are seconds, all chosen in step 7 from the numbers of T1 (the memory of the operators and of the old-generation pool), T5 (the busy threads) and T6 (the overshoot of the in-flight check).
- The test fixture: `TomcatSetup` fixes the `CATALINA_OPTS` of the child JVMs to one tag and writes `server.xml` from `TomcatSampleServer.xml`, which declares an `AccessLogValve` and no `Context`, no other `Valve` and no `backgroundProcessorDelay`. The fixture takes extra JVM options for the child JVMs (heap and the options of the first layer) and lets a test set the `backgroundProcessorDelay` and the valve attributes of its `server.xml` and read the exit status of a child that ended (today the fixture uses the child `Process` only to stop it), so the integration checks can bound the heap and use thresholds of a second.
- Audit of the retrieval endpoints for allocation that grows with the request (`getData` single and multi, `getDataAtTime`, `PvaGetPVData`, the BPL actions with a count or a limit), classified; a finding outside the loops above becomes its own row.
- `retrieval.md` and the installation page state: the protection and its layers; the errors and their codes; the JVM options, with a dump that can be larger than the heap and a new file at each exit, and that the launcher ends the whole appliance while an instance of the installation page ends alone; the valves, where they are declared and what a deployment changes, and that the interrupt is late by up to the background delay; that the protection needs explicit garbage collection, so `-XX:+DisableExplicitGC` is not set; that a PVAccess call that is refused or stopped gets no answer, so a PVAccess client sets a timeout; the sentence of `retrieval.md` about exhausting memory is replaced; and the sentence of `retrieval.md` that says PVAccess retrieval fails the call with the same message (line 204, written for #53) states what the caller sees instead, no answer until its own timeout.

Out of scope: a library for concurrency or rate limiting (D50); a fixed upper bound of an operator argument (the check of #53 rejects a non-number, zero and a negative value only; the bound of this row comes from the budget); requests whose declared size fits the budget and that run while there is no memory pressure, for which the protection changes nothing; the management, engine and ETL code beyond the JVM options and the valve (the audit lists risks there, and the fixes become rows); the analyzer, which takes these layers as a requirement of its design (M62); a load test on the kept appliance.

##### Completion Criteria

- A request of the query class of the summary, at an argument whose declared size T1 finds exceeds the budget, is refused at admission with HTTP 400 and an error that names the budget, without an `OutOfMemoryError`, and the retrieval application answers the next request; a request in flight while the memory after garbage collection is above the second threshold is stopped with an error that names the condition when its allocation since its start exceeds the floor, and the application answers the next request.
- A streaming request that holds little memory, such as a raw read of a long range of 1 Hz data at the heap of the fixture, completes while there is no memory pressure, even when its allocation is larger than the heap.
- While the memory after garbage collection stays above the admission threshold, even after the check has requested a collection, new requests are refused with HTTP 503 and a message that names the condition; once the data that caused the state is released, the next request is accepted without any other load on the JVM.
- A retrieval JVM started with `-XX:+DisableExplicitGC` logs a WARN at start that names the option and its effect on the memory check.
- Requests above the concurrency of the valve are answered 503 at once, and a request that runs past the interrupt threshold stops at its next check.
- At the chosen concurrency, the integration set and the console pages run without a 503 from the valve.
- With the JVM options on by default, the requests of the first criterion, including an argument near 2^31, are refused or stopped without any `OutOfMemoryError` being thrown, so the JVM keeps running.
- A retrieval JVM that throws an `OutOfMemoryError` ends with exit status 3 and a heap dump in its logs folder; the launcher prints `ERROR: Component exited: retrieval; see its console.log`, stops the other three and leaves `status` at `stopped`.
- The values follow the maximum heap: the same request is accepted on a deployment with a larger heap.
- The memory check and the memory bound apply to HTTP retrieval and PVAccess retrieval alike; the valves cover HTTP, and the way the PVAccess server bounds concurrent calls is recorded.
- A test with a limited heap fails on the old code and passes on the new one.
- A request stopped while its answer is being built is not answered as if complete, for the pressure check and for a failed preallocation: the HTTP client gets an error status while the response is not committed and can tell that the answer was stopped once it is, by the connection closed, and the PVAccess call gets no answer, so its caller ends at its own timeout, while the retrieval log names the condition.
- The audit list is recorded in this detail, with every candidate classified.
- `retrieval.md` and the installation page state what the last item of the scope lists, and the book builds with no broken link.
- The default suite, the static checks and the integration set pass.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- D49 (Decision Date 2026-10-20): before the merge of `modernize`; on by default; the values set after measurement.
- D50 (Decision Date 2026-10-20): JDK and Tomcat facilities only, no library; its clause that the request is bounded by its measured allocation is replaced by D52.
- D52 (Decision Date 2026-10-21): the memory bound of a request is its declared size at admission and the memory pressure while it runs, not its cumulative allocation, which counts bytes allocated and not bytes held; the allocation of the request thread only chooses which request stops under pressure.
- Behavioral constraint: the values depend on the heap of the deployment, so they are fixed only after T1 has measured the consumers, T5 the busy threads and T6 the overshoot of the in-flight check; T3 runs before the checks of step 6 exist, because those checks stop the query before the heap is exhausted.
- GC-request decision (Decision Date 2026-10-22): use current old-generation usage as an additional trigger for the rate-limited explicit collection in admission and in-flight checks. Keep collection usage as the only memory value deciding rejection, retain the shared collection interval and allocation floor, and preserve collection-based recovery after load is released. This is the accepted and authorized option 1; production threshold selection remains step 7. Verify stale collection usage with real JVM allocations, garbage recovery without rejection, rate limiting, the real PB pressure matrix, and fractional behavior at different heaps.
- HTTP cancellation decision (Decision Date 2026-10-22): option 1 is accepted and implementation is authorized. HTTP retrieval owns a monotonic deadline from servlet entry, using the positive maximum of the existing stuck and interrupt threshold system properties (600/900 seconds by default); either nonpositive setting disables it, matching valve enablement. A request-local cancellation state persists after an interrupt is consumed and is shared with the per-appliance getDataAtTime workers without resetting the deadline. Check cancellation at event, output and completion boundaries; return 503 before commit and abort an incomplete response after commit. Retain standard valves and WAR-only deployment. This changes T7 from requiring a valve interrupt before every stop to requiring deadline enforcement independently of a background tick, plus a case with an actual consumed interrupt. A cooperative check cannot terminate a permanently blocked I/O operation; stopping within five seconds is qualified only for the bounded reader-pause cases. No watchdog, forced socket closure, PVA deadline or memory-policy change is authorized by this decision.
- T6 closure and T7/T8 scope decision (Decision Date 2026-10-22): close T6 on its completed class, endpoint-preparation and measurement evidence, including 25 functional checks at 2 GiB. The corrected-code PB pressure matrices ran at 256 MiB, not 2 GiB. Carry the retained OOM, measured overshoot and unqualified production settings into step 7 and T7/T8 without claiming that the historical OOM was fixed. Incorporate the JDK memory-threshold facilities and GC behavior documented below into the real HTTP/PVAccess qualification. This decision authorizes that preparation and qualification; it does not select a different production collector or replace polling with a notification listener.
- Work ordering proposed on 2026-10-21: finish T5 at step 5 using the existing valve and fixture code; finish T6 at step 6 with explicit measurement settings and an observed setting that stops accumulating work without an OutOfMemoryError; use the completed T1, T5 and T6 measurements to choose the shipped values in step 7, then run T7 and T8. T5 does not require the step 6 request check or the final values, and T6 does not require a value that step 7 has yet to choose. The full-integration measurement at step 5 supplies input to step 7; the final full-suite regression remains T10.
- Behavioral dependencies of the revised checks: the request's stop at the next interrupt check belongs to T6 (the protection class) and T7 (the real HTTP path); normal console requests at the selected concurrency and the repeated valve scenarios belong to T7; normal integration traffic at the selected concurrency belongs to T10. These checks remain required for M85 completion after T5 closes.
- Measurement boundary: the fixture's JMX sampler reads the shared connector of the JVM hosting all four applications. Record its aggregate maximum, sample count and workload coverage in T5; that aggregate is the conservative input to step 7, not separate measured maxima for management and retrieval. The whole-set measurement and concurrent console requests use placeholder valve values, before the final values are selected.
- Behavioral constraint: memory exhaustion is forced only on a retrieval JVM that a test starts, never on the kept appliance.
- Behavioral constraint: with the JVM options every `OutOfMemoryError` ends the JVM, including the errors that today are caught per request and the VM-limit error of an argument near 2^31, which needs no full heap, so one such request would end the whole appliance under the launcher. The launcher and the installation page therefore get the options in the same change as the declared-size check and the pressure checks of step 6, and until then the options are set only in the fixture for T3 (observed 2026-10-21, JDK 21).
- Behavioral constraint: the observation came from a series of requests over about nine hours, not from one request; T1 establishes whether one request exhausts the heap of the fixture, and T3 sends the request, or the sequence, that T1 found.
- Behavioral constraint: the valve concurrency of management and retrieval counts the calls the other web applications make, and the interrupt of the stuck-thread valve is late by up to the `backgroundProcessorDelay` of the container, so step 7 chooses the interrupt threshold at or above the threshold with that lateness in mind; the concurrency comes from the busy threads that T5 samples, because the valve counts every request of its context, and the thresholds come from the measurement of T1 and the reading of T2.
- Behavioral constraint: the values of step 7 let two requests that each fit the budget leave, together, a usage after a collection above the admission threshold and below the second threshold at the heap of the integration fixture, because T7 produces the refused state that way without stopping the two (no test-only setting, D49).
- Behavioral constraint: the in-flight check stops a request later than the moment its live data crosses the second threshold, because the usage after collection changes only at an old-generation collection and the collection request is rate limited: in a probe on a 256 MB G1 heap with one map entry per bin, the stop came 10 to 61 MB above the threshold, and with 85% and a check every 100,000 events 5 MB below the maximum heap (observed on 2026-10-21 on JDK 21). With the JVM options on, a stop that comes too late is an `OutOfMemoryError` that ends the JVM, so the headroom between the second threshold and the maximum heap exceeds the overshoot that T6 measures at the heap of the fixture.
- Behavioral constraint: the observations of 2026-10-21 in this detail came from small programs outside the repository; T3 rechecks the JVM options, T5 the valve timings, T6 the usage after collection, the collection request and the effect of `DisableExplicitGC`, T8 what a PVAccess caller sees, T1 the allocation of a raw read and the collection pause, and T6 the overshoot.
- Owner decision 2026-10-20: the delivery of an error raised while the answer is being built is part of step 6, together with the catch blocks that swallow it in both paths and the null guard after a failed preallocation, because the pressure check of the streams throws inside that pipeline and would otherwise never reach the client.
- Owner decisions, each recorded here with its date when made: (1) the error of a request whose declared size is over the budget: HTTP 400, because the client can shrink the request, while the memory check and the valve answer 503, because waiting helps (Decision Date 2026-10-21; the alternative was 503 for all three); the PVAccess call is failed with the same message, which its caller sees as decision (4) states. (2) How a mid-stream error reaches the HTTP client once the response is committed: the connection is closed so that the body is cut short, which any HTTP client tells from a complete answer in every format; an error record at the end of the body is left out because the nine formats have no place for it, and swallowing the error, as the servlet does today, shows a complete 200 (Decision Date 2026-10-21, from the evidence of T2). (3) Where the valves are declared: a `META-INF/context.xml` in each of the retrieval and management WARs, so that no operator step is needed; `server.xml` and the `conf/context.xml` of an instance are left out because an operator would edit one file per instance (Decision Date 2026-10-21, from the evidence of T2). (4) What a PVAccess caller sees when its call is refused or stopped: no answer until its own timeout, with the message in the log of the client library, as that library behaves; the alternative, an answer that carries the refusal in a result structure, is left out because it changes the shape of the PVAccess answer (Decision Date 2026-10-21).
- Valve regression decision (Decision Date 2026-10-23): the application deadline of a retrieval request, derived from the stuck and interrupt thresholds, replaces the StuckThreadDetectionValve record as what the valve regression expects for a long request. With the thresholds equal, the deadline stops the request before the valve records it, so `ValveConcurrencyTest` asserts the concurrency refusal and the deadline stop (503 naming the deadline within the threshold window). The deadline keeps its definition as the positive maximum of the two thresholds; no test asserts a StuckThreadDetectionValve record for a retrieval request after this change.
- External-proxy stage decision (Decision Date 2026-10-23): the stage of `getDataAtTime` that calls an external appliance is corrected under M85, as the engine stage was, because the review reproduced the same wait without a deadline there; the stage owns its HTTP calls and waits with the original deadline. M55 keeps the verification of the proxy against a real second appliance; multi-appliance cases stay out of scope (D23, D26).
- Snapshot worker fallback decision (Decision Date 2026-10-23): the snapshot store workers keep registering no estimate. With the thread allocation counter available, a worker is stopped under memory pressure by its measured allocation; without the counter it is not, which is accepted for the OpenJDK (HotSpot) runtime of this fork, and the limit stays recorded in this register.
- Values from measurement, set in step 7: the fractions of the heap (the budget, the admission threshold, the second threshold), the allocation floor, the check interval N, the interval of the collection request, the valve concurrency and the two stuck thresholds.

###### Shared JDK qualification contract for T7 and T8

This contract extends both network checks above. T6 is closed on its recorded scope; the results below remain pending until the real HTTP and PVAccess paths run. The first qualification uses the existing JDK 21 G1 configuration. Collector comparisons and notification observations inform the production decision; a diagnostic result alone does not qualify a deployment configuration.

The JDK provides polling and threshold notifications, including an example that stops accepting work above a memory threshold and resumes below it [1]. The notification delivery time is not guaranteed, and support must be checked per pool. The API describes workload control, not recovery from exhausted memory [2]. The existing implementation polls these beans; observing a notification does not establish that the application refused a request.

| JDK mechanism | Required observation in the real request scenario |
| --- | --- |
| `MemoryPoolMXBean` usage and collection usage [1], [2] | Record actual pool names, threshold support, current usage and collection usage. Correlate threshold crossings, any observed notifications, application rejection and recovery. Measure notification delay if notifications are evaluated; do not rely on an assumed immediate callback or a downward notification. |
| G1 adaptive IHOP and `G1ReservePercent` [3] | Retain effective options and GC logs for the baseline. Attribute any later change in GC timing, pauses or remaining heap to an otherwise comparable run; reserve space is for GC and is not a reservation for a query. |
| `ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent` and `DisableExplicitGC` [3] | Check the effect on the production guard's collection reading, refusal and recovery. A returning `System.gc()` call alone is not evidence that the required pool value has refreshed. Keep the disabled-GC warning/recovery diagnostic separate from supported production acceptance. |
| ZGC `SoftMaxHeapSize` and allocation stalls [4], [5] | Before any comparison, verify the installed JDK's exact ZGC mode, supported pools and compatibility with the production guard. Record effective soft and hard limits, allocation stalls and request outcomes. A stall is waiting for allocation, not an application refusal; unsupported startup is a compatibility result, not successful protection. |
| `ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` and `HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError` [6], [7] | Retain JVM exit status and dump evidence if OOM occurs. An OOM exit fails the prevention case even if termination and dump creation work as specified; T3 remains the separate evidence for post-OOM behavior. |

Execute the following through built WARs and the shipped store/postprocessor paths, without replacing internal allocation or admission code:

1. Record JDK identity, effective options, maximum and initial heap, selected pools, protection settings, WAR/source identities, request parameters and generated-store identity. Verify that startup actually activates protection before submitting load. Check current host and process limits before scheduling a larger heap; run resource-intensive profiles sequentially on fixture-owned JVMs.
2. Establish a single accumulating request that fits its declared budget and a normal request that succeeds. Submit overlapping accumulating requests from external clients, proving their overlap and actual memory growth. For PVA, use separate TCP connections so a serial receive thread does not conceal concurrency. Retain a memory-admission case below the HTTP valve limit, distinct from valve-overload rejection.
3. While measured memory is above admission, submit another request and verify HTTP 503 with the memory condition, or the agreed PVA failure/log/timeout behavior. Separately drive the in-flight pressure condition and verify the bounded stop, correct transport failure and continued JVM service. A configured load, a valve 503 or an OOM exit does not establish memory admission or pressure protection.
4. Release the load and verify a subsequent real request succeeds without a restart or an unrelated allocating workload. Preserve the no-pressure streaming control; PVA's retained response is measured separately from HTTP streaming. Check the same fixed query across heaps for budget scaling, and scale accumulating input separately when testing pressure so a larger heap does not silently remove fault exposure.
5. Cover a bounded small heap and 2 GiB, then a larger heap after the capacity check. Record the exact heap/profile/workload combinations before each run; do not extrapolate the 256 MiB overshoot to another heap or collector. Retain GC activity, pauses/stalls, total heap and collection usage, minimum observed remaining heap, response status/body completeness, request start/end and refusal/recovery times, child lifetime and native outcome. Sampled peaks and non-atomic reads are observations, not guaranteed bounds.
6. Before a long run, rehearse one bounded end-to-end case through capture, normal finish and final evaluation. Declare per-case request deadlines, recovery deadlines, required headroom, evidence location and stop conditions after the baseline measurements and before judging candidates. Missing overlap, missing pressure or missing terminal evidence is Incomplete; OOM or an incorrect complete response is Failed. Preserve failed candidates and the historical OOM. Qualify final settings only when both T7 and T8 satisfy their full contracts, including existing valve/console and transport requirements.

Startup activation, coupled launcher/installation options and the initial real-network fixtures are implemented; the remaining work is full network and collector qualification. The JDK findings do not authorize replacing the protection algorithm or selecting ZGC as the production collector. Such a change requires a concrete compatibility/behavior result and a separate decision; until then the accepted polling design is the baseline.

T1 measured values, 2026-10-21. Each request ran the path of the servlet: the post processor found by name, initialized and asked for its estimate, the plain PB store returning the wrapped callables, each callable run on the calling thread, the answer written as JSON, the consolidated stream and the final data written last. The data is one PV, 1 Hz, 30 days at the end of which every request ends; a range of 80 days reaches 50 days before the data. Allocation is `getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes` over the request; held is the heap after full collections minus the heap before the request, while the post processor and the consumer are still referenced; needed is the smallest heap of 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1536 and 2048 MB at which the request was answered.
